ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating KL-Regularized Fine-Tuning of Diffusion Models with Synthetic Data
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a pre-trained DDPM [1] on the CIFAR-10 [2] dataset using the KL-regularized objective, replacing the marginal KL divergence with a relaxation that approximates the KL divergence between entire denoising trajectories. Compare the performance to a baseline that ignores the KL regularization.
CONTROLS: Baseline: DDPM fine-tuned without KL regularization, Ablations: using only the reward for fine-tuning, using a different relaxation for the KL divergence.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: The KL-regularized fine-tuning should lead to more stable training and slightly better results than the baseline, but the performance could be subpar due to the initial value function bias problem.

[1] Ho et al. "Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models" (2020)
[2] Krizhevsky et al. "Learning Multiple Layers of Features from Tiny Images" (2009)

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Evaluating Multi-Step Fine-Tuning for Diffusion Models with Document Layout Generation
PROPOSAL: Fine-tune a pre-trained DDPM [1] on the InkML [2] dataset using a multi-step fine-tuning approach that adaptively updates the denoising objective at each step based on the previously generated samples. PREDICTION: Multi-step fine-tuning could lead to better performance than KL-regularized fine-tuning by leveraging the sequence structure of document layout generation, but the improvement may be modest if the pre-trained model is already well-suited for this task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Initial Value Function Bias Problem in KL-Regularized Fine-Tuning of Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the initial value function bias problem in KL-regularized fine-tuning of diffusion models, and propose a new approach to mitigate this issue by adjusting the KL regularization term based on the effective sample size of the pre-trained model. Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments will be conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard KL-regularized fine-tuning, Theoretical analysis:derive the bias-variance tradeoff in KL-regularized fine-tuning, Ablations: varying the effective sample size factor.
COST: 68000
PREDICTION: The proposed approach could lead to a significant reduction in the initial value function bias problem, resulting in improved fine-tuning performance, but the improvement may be difficult to achieve in practice if the pre-trained model is highly optimized.

(Paper classification: Theory only)

TITLE: Investigating the Relationship Between KL-Regularized Reward Maximization and Policy Gradient Methods for Diffusion Model Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Investigate the relationship between KL-regularized reward maximization and policy gradient methods for diffusion model fine-tuning by analyzing the asymptotic behavior of both approaches. A theoretical framework will be developed to compare the convergence rates and optimality of both methods, and the results will be validated through numerical experiments.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard KL-regularized fine-tuning and policy gradient methods, Theoretical analysis: derive the convergence rates and optimality of both methods.
COST: 93600
PREDICTION: The theoretical framework could provide valuable insights into the relationship between KL-regularized reward maximization and policy gradient methods, but the practical implications of the results may be limited if the pre-trained model is not well-suited for fine-tuning.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Infeasible KL-Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the impact of ignoring the KL regularization for diffusion models, quantifying the effects of unstable training behavior on sample quality and computational costs.
CONTROLS: Compare against a diffusion model fine-tuned solely on the reward objective, which serves as a baseline for the feasibility of ignoring KL regularization.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: This would lead to unstable training, especially in large-scale settings, with noticeable degradation in sample quality, and an expected increase in computational costs due to retraining the model from scratch. However, it might highlight that this instability may be circumvented using smaller model initializations and using the diffusion model without KL regularization until the policy diverges from the pre-trained model, or other chasing KL-regularized training with smaller KL regularization weights when the gradients get larger.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Trajectory KL Regularization Fisher Estimation
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical estimator based on Fishers identity to approximate the marginal KL divergence between the fine-tuned and pre-trained diffusion models, leveraging the lower-triangular Fisher information matrix computed from a pre-trained diffusion model's noisy samples and their policy gradient wrt. the reward objectives.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed Fisher estimator against the existing KL divergence approximation between entire denoising trajectories, using a diffusion model fine-tuned with this method.
COST: 2259
PREDICTION: The proposed Fisher estimation approach should result in more accurate KL divergence approximations compared to the existing method. However, potential challenges include accurately relating Fisher matrix elements to the computed gradients and stabilizing the numerical computation of Fisher inverse.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Denoising Path KL Regularization with Reward-Weighted Importances

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Fine-tuning Diffusion Models with KL-regularized Reward Maximization using Stochastic Trajectory Sampling
PROPOSAL: We propose a new method for fine-tuning diffusion models using KL-regularized reward maximization. Instead of computing the KL divergence between entire denoising trajectories, we will sample a fixed number of stochastic trajectories at each time step and compute the KL divergence between these sample trajectories and the reference model's trajectories. We will use PPO to maximize the expected reward while minimizing the KL divergence. We will experiment with different sampling strategies, such as uniform sampling, importance sampling, and stratified sampling. We will evaluate our method on text-to-image generation, document layout generation, and molecule generation tasks using widely recognized metrics such as Inception Score, FID Score, and Success Rate.
CONTROLS: We will compare our method to two baselines: (1) PPO without KL regularization, and (2) PPO with KL regularization using entire denoising trajectories.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: Our method will outperform both baselines on all three tasks and will exhibit stable training behavior, especially on large-scale settings. However, it might fail to capture the errors in the initial value function, leading to subpar results for some datasets.

We will experiment with different flow architectures and ensemble methods.

TITLE:  REVISED Efficient KL-Regularized Fine-Tuning with Flow-Based KL Estimation
PROPOSAL: Inspired by the flow model structure, we propose to derive an unbiased and efficient estimate of the marginal KL divergence between the pre-trained diffusion distribution and the reference distribution using recent flow-based methods such as Normalizing Flows for Inference (NFI). We extend the original proposal by including a robust estimation of the flow-based KL divergence by accounting for the uncertainty in the flow dynamics via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo, but also investigate the potential benefits of pre-training the NFI network on a proxy task, such as denoising a related dataset, to improve its capacity to learn complex flow dynamics.
CONTROLS: Same as original; adds two additional baselines: one where we pre-train the NFI network on the denoising task, and another where we only pre-train on the NFI objective without any prior task.
COST: 23300
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in robustness and accuracy of the KL estimation, as well as potential reduction in number of iterations required to reach a stable fine-tuning objective; potential trade-off between pre-training on proxy task and fine-tuning on target task, and potential increased sensitivity to choice of pre-training task.

TITLE:  Multi-Step KL-Regularized Fine-Tuning with HMC-Injected Flow-Based KL Estimation
PROPOSAL: We propose a multi-step approach that iteratively refines the fine-tuning objective by progressively refining the estimated marginal KL divergence between the pre-trained diffusion distribution and the reference distribution. At each refinement step, we inject the flow-based KL estimation with Hamiltonian Monte Carlo to better capture the uncertainty in the flow dynamics. We also investigate the benefits of adding a regularizer to the refinement objective to encourage more stable and accurate KL estimates.
CONTROLS: Hold out the multi-step refinement steps and compare performance against single-step refinement.

PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to estimating and correcting errors of pre-trained flow models using data samples from the target distribution, without any explicit reward signal. We also investigate the benefits of using multiple flows and weight averaging to improve the accuracy and stability of the error correction process.

TITLE: Scalable and Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large-Scale Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to scalable and efficient fine-tuning of large-scale diffusion models by leveraging distributed learning, batch-based KL regularization, and network pruning techniques. Specifically, we divide the fine-tuning process into smaller batches, optimize each batch in parallel using a distributed learning framework, and prune the model to reduce computational overhead. We also investigate the benefits of using transfer learning to fine-tune smaller sub-networks of the original model.
CONTROLS: Compare with decentralized approaches, heterognous distributed approaches, and core-surbasket architectures.
COST: 100000
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in scalability and efficiency of the fine-tuning process due to the distributed and batch-based approaches, but potential increased complexity due to synchronization of communication between learners; possibility of suboptimal convergence due to pruning and transferring sub-network knowledge.

PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to estimating and correcting errors of pre-trained flow models using data samples from the target distribution, without any explicit reward signal. Specifically, we use a probabilistic model to estimate the error in the pre-trained flow model and then correct it by adjusting the flow parameters to match the target distribution. We also investigate the benefits of using multiple flows and weight averaging to improve the accuracy and stability of the error correction process.
CONTROLS: Compare with standard fine-tuning and KL-regularized fine-tuning baselines.
COST: 200000
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in accuracy and stability of the pre-trained flow model due to the error correction mechanism, but potential increased computational cost due to the additional training and optimization steps; possibility of over-correction and decreased generalizability if not used judiciously.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scalable and Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large-Scale Diffusion Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to scalable and efficient fine-tuning of large-scale diffusion models by leveraging distributed learning, batch-based KL regularization, and network pruning techniques. Specifically, we divide the fine-tuning process into smaller batches, optimize each batch in parallel using a distributed learning framework, and prune the model to reduce computational overhead. We also investigate the benefits of using transfer learning to fine-tune smaller sub-networks of the original model.
CONTROLS: Compare with decentralized approaches, heterognous distributed approaches, and core-surbasket architectures.
COST: 300000
PREDICTION: Expected improvement in scalability and efficiency of the fine-tuning process due to the distributed and batch-based approaches, but potential increased complexity due to synchronization of communication between learners; possibility of suboptimal convergence due to pruning and transferring sub-network knowledge.

TITLE: Revisiting KL Regularization for Diffusion Models with Trajectory Upper Bounds
PROPOSAL: We will experimentally compare the fine-tuning performance of a pre-trained diffusion model based on two different KL regularization approaches for real-world data: (1) ignoring the KL term and freeing the variational distribution, and (2) using a trajectory upper bound for the KL divergence between entire denoising trajectories to constrain the learning problem. We will use the reimplement PPCL (PPO with Pathwise KL control) proposed by Fort et al. (2022) for the latter, and adapt it for diffusion models.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Exploiting Generative Structure for More Effective Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: We will extend the ETD-based fine-tuning method by incorporating a learnable time-dependent penalty term. This penalty term will be used to compute a more data-efficient differentiable regularization that encourages the model to produce samples that transition smoothly through the denoising steps. We will explore different forms for the penalty term, including exponential and polynomial functions, and examine their effect on fine-tuning performance.

CONTROLS: We will compare the updated ETD-based method against regular KL regularization, ignoring the KL term, and the baseline of using a fixed penalty term. We will also investigate the performance of the method on different types of diffusion models and datasets, including image and molecule generation.

COST: 4838.4 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: I expect the learnable time-dependent penalty term to improve the fine-tuning performance by reducing the gap between the target data distribution and the generated denoising trajectories. However, the choice of the penalty function may require careful tuning, and the method may fail if the penalty term is too dominant, limiting the model's ability to explore the reward space.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Correcting Pre-Training Errors without Explicit Reward
PROPOSAL: We will investigate whether pre-trained flow models can be corrected to match the target data distribution without explicit reward feedback. We will use a combination of metrics, including visual inspection, Frechet Inception Distance (FID), and Kernel Inception Distance (KID), to assess the quality of the generated samples. Additionally, we will explore the use of self-supervised learning objectives, such as reconstruction and autoencoding tasks, to regularize the model and encourage it to produce samples that are more aligned with the target data distribution.

CONTROLS: We will compare our proposed method against the baseline of fine-tuning the pre-trained model using explicit reward feedback. We will also investigate the performance of different self-supervised learning objectives and their combinations.

COST: 6400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: I expect the correction of pre-training errors to be possible without explicit reward feedback, and that the combination of metrics will provide a more comprehensive understanding of the generated samples' quality. However, the choice of self-supervised learning objective may require careful tuning, and the method may fail if the objective is too weak or too strong, leading to underfitting or overfitting.

PROPOSAL: We will propose an adaptive sampling method that adjusts the number and type of samples used for fine-tuning based on the current training progress and the model's performance. CONTROLS: We will compare our adaptive sampling method against traditional sampling strategies, including random sampling and sampling based on uniform distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Parameter Steering for Fine-Grained Behavior Control
PROPOSAL: We investigate a new steering method called "MPS" that concatenates multiple interchangeable steering primitives, including addition and ablation, and predicates over a control vector that scales each primitive's impact. We hypothesize that through preemptive transforms that apply optimal scaling factors for each layer and apply negative transformations to amortize costs for common projection forms, MPS can grant fine-grained control over target behaviors, enabling the transition between strong expression, partial suppression, removal, and inversion. Experimental validation will compare MPS against state-of-the-art steering methods on emotional text generation tasks (e.g. anger, fear) and refusal of harmful requests (e.g. self-harm, hate speech).
CONTROLS: We will control for comparison with orthogonal ablation, activation addition with uniform scaling, and a baseline of neural inputs without any steering.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate MPS to yield performance comparable to or better than competitive techniques on evaluated tasks, though the model may struggle with excessive steering on complex emotional outputs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Stein Priors for Robust Steering
PROPOSAL: We draw inspiration from Bayesian neural networks and employ the Stein Prior to achieve robust steering by minimizing the expected information gain with respect to a reference distribution. The reference distribution can be learned from either data or expert knowledge. This method leverages the underlying structure of the model via a variational Stein process, reducing the dependence on layer-specific scales and specific steering primitives, resulting in a simplified and universal control parameter.
CONTROLS: We compare the performance of the proposed method against ROM (Meta-ROM) on several real-world tasks, as well as against the state-of-the-art steering methods on emotional text generation and refusal of harmful requests.
COST: 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Stein Priors may provide a more robust control mechanism due to its ability to generalize across different layers and steering primitives, but it might struggle with short-circuiting the underlying risk during posterior handling, potentially resulting in poor performance on very difficult behaviors.

TITLE: Bayesian Model-Agnostic Steering for Transfer Across Behaviors
PROPOSAL: We propose a Bayesian formulation of the steering problem that enables seamless transfer of steering mechanisms across different behaviors, models, and even tasks. Our method, "BAS-T", extends the existing steering paradigms with a Bayesian neural network learning framework, allowing the model to acquire task-agnostic steering capabilities through expectation-maximization.
CONTROLS: We compare BAS-T with ROM (Meta-ROM), Stein Priors, OrthoCode, and C-Steer on a wide range of real-world tasks and behavioral scenarios, including generalization across different models, tasks, and datasets.
COST: 1800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: BAS-T has the potential to unlock significant advances in steering robustness, generalizability, and transferability. However, the increased computational complexity and requirement for explicit prior knowledge might hinder its applicability to certain settings or resource-constrained environments.

TITLE: Selective Steering through Information-Theoretic Beam Search
PROPOSAL: We introduce a selective steering approach based on information-theoretic beam search, allowing the model to probe and iteratively select the most relevant steering primitives for a given task or behavior. Our method, "i-Search", employs a variational information bottleneck to optimize the trade-off between steering precision and generalization, ensuring that only the most informative primitives are retained.
CONTROLS: We evaluate i-Search on several real-world tasks, including emotional text generation and refusal of harmful requests, and compare its performance with current state-of-the-art steering methods, including ROM (Meta-ROM), Stein Priors, OrthoCode, C-Steer, and BAS-T.
COST: 2400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: i-Search has the potential to significantly improve steering performance by providing a principled and data-efficient mechanism for selective primitive selection. However, its effectiveness may be limited by the complexity of the problem space and the accuracy of the variational information bottleneck approximation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sanity Checks on the Orthogonality of Feature Directions
PROPOSAL: Due to the limitations of directional ablation operations in ignoring partial alignment with the target feature direction, we investigate the orthogonality of feature directions learned from contrastive examples using various metrics (e.g., dot product correlation, cosine similarity) and statistical tests (e.g., Kolmogorov-Smirnov test) on synthetic and real-world datasets. This will shed light on whether feature directions really are (nearly) orthogonal and how often feature redundancy occurs.
CONTROLS: Compare between different metrics and statistical tests, study the impact of training data size, and experiment with modified training objectives to enforce orthogonality.
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: While we expect feature directions to be highly correlated, due to the limitations of contrastive learning, we anticipate some degree of feature redundancy, particularly when the target behaviors exhibit strong relationships or the dataset has label noise.

TITLE: Designing Parameterized Steering Primitives
PROPOSAL: To overcome the limitations of existing steering primitives, we propose a new set of parameterized primitives that can adapt to the specific layer and steering context. Specifically, we introduce two new primitives: learnable scaling of additive steering and adaptive orthogonal projection for ablation. These new primitives will be trained end-to-end along with the baseline steering operations on a suite of labeled datasets.
CONTROLS: Evaluate our new primitives against existing steering methods on a range of tasks and models, and compare with a baseline that uses fixed parameters for the new primitives.
COST: 48600
PREDICTION: The new primitives should exhibit improved performance and robustness on steering tasks, but may require careful task-specific tuning and could fail to generalize to new tasks or models if not properly regularized.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continuously Controlled Steering with Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to steering using contrastive learning objectives that do not rely on binary labels or specific behavior labels. Instead, we use autoencoding and reconstructive objectives to steer the model's behavior gradually, with the control parameter determining the closeness of the reconstructed activation to the original, steering towards or away from a target behavior. This approach aims to provide a fine-grained and coherent control over model behavior.
CONTROLS: Evaluate our approach on a suite of tasks and models, and compare with parameterized steering primitives, existing steering methods, and a baseline that relies on externally provided behavior labels.
COST: 9000
PREDICTION: Our approach should achieve smooth and coherent control over model behavior, but may require significant computational resources for training and may struggle to capture complex or nuanced behaviors.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Revised: Continuously Controlled Steering with Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We modify our proposal to incorporate an adaptation of our contrastive learning approach to handle the RMS normalization regime, by modifying the autoencoding objective to account for the fixed activation norm. This will enable us to analyze the interaction between the contrastive learning objective and normalization in a more principled manner.
CONTROLS: Evaluate our revised approach on a range of tasks and models, and compare with parameterized steering primitives, existing steering methods, and a baseline that relies on externally provided behavior labels.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: By accounting for RMS normalization in our contrastive learning approach, we expect to improve the coherence and effectiveness of our control mechanism, particularly in regimes where normalization is most prevalent. However, we may encounter difficulties in precisely calibrating the control parameter in such regimes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Steering Methods on Real-World LLM Safety Tasks
PROPOSAL: We extend our evaluation to real-world LLM safety tasks, specifically refusal of harmful requests (jailbreaking) and emotion control of generated text. We compare the new steering methods (parameterized primitives and continuously controlled steering with contrastive learning) with existing methods on these tasks using large-scale real-world datasets. This will provide a more comprehensive assessment of the proposed methods and their applicability to real-world safety scenarios.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the methods on a variety of LLM architectures and safety datasets, and compare with baselines that use existing steering methods and no steering at all.
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: Our new steering methods should exhibit improved performance and safety on the real-world tasks, particularly in terms of fine-grained control and coherence. However, we may encounter difficulties in scaling our methods to very large models or datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of RMS Normalization on Activation Steering
PROPOSAL: Analyze the effect of RMS normalization on the behavior of activation addition and directional ablation steering primitives. Specifically, examine the interaction between steering edits and the fixed activation norm enforced by RMS normalization. We will design a set of experiments comparing activation addition with and without accounting for the normalized activation, as well as different variations of directional ablation under various normalization regimes.
CONTROLS: Compare to a baseline where no normalization is applied, as well as ablations where only addition or ablation is applied without accounting for normalization.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: We expect that accounting for the normalized activation will improve the effectiveness and coherence of the steering operations, but also render them more sensitive to slight variations in the input or actual layer scales, potentially defeating the initial intuition of a simple-to-set control parameter.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sanity Checks on the Orthogonality of Feature Directions
PROPOSAL: Due to the limitations of directional ablation operations in ignoring partial alignment with the target feature direction, we investigate the orthogonality of feature directions learned from contrastive examples using various metrics (e.g., dot product correlation, cosine similarity) and statistical tests (e.g., Kolmogorov-Smirnov test) on synthetic and real-world datasets. This will shed light on whether feature directions really are (nearly) orthogonal and how often feature redundancy occurs.
CONTROLS: Compare between different metrics and statistical tests, study the impact of training data size, and experiment with modified training objectives to enforce orthogonality.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: While we expect feature directions to be highly correlated, due to the limitations of contrastive learning, we anticipate some degree of feature redundancy, particularly when the target behaviors exhibit strong relationships or the dataset has label noise.

The goal is to develop a theoretical framework explaining how normalization influences the effectiveness and sensitivity of steering operations.
CONTROLS: Compare our expressed model with existing steering primitives, evaluate robustness against perturbations in the activation norm and study implications for setting the control parameter.
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: With our new framework, we expect to provide a principled approach to analyzing steering operations under normalization, but may encounter challenges in extending our model to deep and complex neural network architectures.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Continuous Activation Steering via Geodesic Movement
PROPOSAL: We propose an alternative to standard activation steering methods by incorporating geodesic movements in activation space. This is achieved by defining a Riemannian manifold over the model's activations and introducing a steering control parameter that adapts along the geodesics connecting different activations. Our aim is to explicitly steer the model toward or away from target behaviors by updating the activations along the shortest path on the manifold.
CONTROLS: Geodesic movement will be compared against the current state-of-the-art methods, including activation addition and directional ablation, as well as a simple distance-based model that moves activations in the direction of a nearest neighbor representing the target behavior.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed geodesic method to provide more nuanced control over model behavior, especially at lower steering strengths, and effectively adapt to varying difficulty of steering tasks, potentially showing its superiority in most of the experiment domains and proposed by performance in maintaining model fluency across negative alignments. However, geodesic computation can be computationally expensive, limiting its applicability to smaller models.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Analyzing the Impact of RMS Normalization on Activation Steering
PROPOSAL: We will theoretically analyze the effect of RMSP normalization on activation steering by viewing it as a transformation in the probabalistic manifold of activations. We will prove that RMS normalization causes transformation-invariant density estimates of activation distributions and explore how this affects the representational power of activation steering methods, including the geodesic approach, by bounding their performance in normalized activation spaces.
CONTROLS: This analytical work will serve as a baseline to understand how RMSP normalization affects the representational space of activation steering methods, and essential in ensuring the proposed experiments are representative of true model behavior in practice.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: By understanding the geometric and probabilistic implications of RMSP normalization, we hope to develop new insights and approaches that combine activation steering with this normalization process to derive more effective and interpretable control methods, possibly guiding further work in context insensitive representation learning of LLMs.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Conditioning Activation Steering for Enhanced Contextual Sensitivity
PROPOSAL: We will explore how to condition activation steering on contextual information, such as input sequences or task labels, to develop more fine-grained control over model behavior. This will involve introducing a novel conditional activation steering module that takes contextual features as input and dynamically adjusts the steering control parameter to adapt to the specific context.
CONTROLS: We will evaluate the performance of this conditional steering method against the geodesic method and simple methods like activation addition, as well as ablation studies to understand the importance of contextual information and the conditional module itself.
COST: 1680
PREDICTION: By conditioning activation steering on contextual information, we expect to significantly improve the controllability and expressiveness of the model, reducing the gap between desired behavior and observed behavior in realistic scenarios, which is a current servicellation of more fine-tuning based-approaches.

TITLE: Developing Steering-Sensitive Model Evaluation Metrics
PROPOSAL: We will design and evaluate new model evaluation metrics that are sensitive to steering controls, allowing for more effective assessment of activation steering methods. These metrics will focus on the model's behavior under different steering conditions, capturing its ability to adapt and generalize in response to the steering controls.

This could also have broader implications for model evaluation and development, potentially enhancing our ability to evaluate and optimize language models.

TITLE: Continuous Activation Steering via Geodesic Movement
PROPOSAL: We propose an alternative to standard activation steering methods by incorporating geodesic movements in activation space. This is achieved by defining a Riemannian manifold over the model's activations and introducing a steering control parameter that adapts along the geodesics connecting different activations. Our aim is to explicitly steer the model toward or away from target behaviors by updating the activations along the shortest path on the manifold.
CONTROLS: Geodesic movement will be compared against the current state-of-the-art methods, including activation addition and directional ablation, as well as a simple distance-based model that moves activations in the direction of a nearest neighbor representing the target behavior.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: We expect the proposed geodesic method to provide more nuanced control over model behavior, especially at lower steering strengths, and effectively adapt to varying difficulty of steering tasks, potentially showing its superiority in most of the experiment domains and proposed by performance in maintaining model fluency across negative alignments. However, geodesic computation can be computationally expensive, limiting its applicability to smaller models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A Bound on Activation Steering's Consistency Across Layers
PROPOSAL: Derive a theoretical bound that guarantees the consistency of activation steering's effect across different layers of a transformer, assuming that the feature directions learned from contrastive examples are approximately linearly separable. Specifically, the bound will determine the maximum magnitude of the feature direction as a function of the model's depth and the gap between the separable clusters. This result provides a theoretical justification for the feasibility of continuous control over layer-specific activation scales with a single, model-agnostic control parameter.
CONTROLS: Empirically evaluate the bound on a selection of widely used pre-trained transformer models (e.g., BERT, RoBERTa).
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The derived bound is tight for moderately deep models (up to 12 layers), but shows diminishing returns for much deeper architectures (>24 layers). The bound's gap to experimental observations might be wider in regimes with sparse or diffused representations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A New Steerable Activation Primitives for Continuous Control
PROPOSAL: Introduce a new activation steering primitive, referred to as joint ablation-addition. This method combines the projection of a feature direction with an addition of a scaled vector orthogonal to the feature direction. Joint ablation-addition can be seen as a diminutive form of the full orthogonalization operation, in that it leaves partial residual features in place, potentially alleviating the 'wipeout' effect present in standard ablation and allowing for partial suppression of the target feature. 
CONTROLS: Compare joint ablation-addition to the original ablation and addition schemes, as well as to existing conditional methods, using standard evaluation metrics (e.g., percentage of informed controllers, freedom from disturbance of general abilities).
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: Joint ablation-addition will yield smoother, more robust control transitions between near-full expression and partial suppression of the target behavior, especially in complex scenes with multiple, relevant features. However, its ability might degrade when the desired and interfering features are highly correlated or hierarchical in the underlying feature space.

TITLE:  Federated Learning with Heterogeneous Task-Specific Models using Shared Autoencoders
PROPOSAL: Conduct a federated multi-task learning experiment where each user has a unique task-specific model, but a shared task-agnostic autoencoder. The autoencoder is shared across all users, and its parameters are updated during each client-server communication round. The task-specific models are then fine-tuned locally on the users' individual data, using the shared autoencoder as a layer in the model architecture.
CONTROLS: As a baseline, use a federated learning method with a customized model for each user, without sharing any parameters. For ablation, conduct the same experiment but without a shared autoencoder, and instead with a global model that serves as a basic encoder for all task-specific models.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The shared autoencoder will provide a good initialization and regularizer for the task-specific models, leading to better task performance compared to the baseline without sharing any parameters, but with possible overfitting to the autoencoder due to the shared layer.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Model-Agnostic Alignment for Federated Multi-Task Learning without Architectural Congruity
PROPOSAL: Experiment on the widely adopted FEMNIST and Shakespeare datasets used in federated multi-task learning benchmarks, where each user can have a different model architecture and task. Evaluate the performance of a model-agnostic alignment method based on a recently proposed geometric interpretation of kernel centered alignments, which ensures the alignment measure remains positive even for representations with different latent spaces. Additionally, incorporate a federated learning setup that supports model updates without exposing local iterations or gradients, to protect user privacy; a trade-off can be made for faster convergence and higher communication efficiency by allowing the server to receive only final model updates and feature statistics. Use a robust average of task-specific loss functions to accommodate the diversity of tasks and user policies.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: users are free to select their own architectures, with standard federated averaging.
Baseline 2: Architectural congruity with known heterogeneous architectures and semi-homogeneous task assignments.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: We expect a 5-10 percent increase in collective accuracy for diverse users over standard federated averaging, with higher model diversity allowing for better representation convergence. However, adding users with significantly different tasks is expected to still cause a noticeable decrease in performance; conclusive results are best obtained when users are selected with moderate task compatibility, aside from personalization tasks.

PROPOSAL: Establish a theoretical framework for proving the convergence of a model-agnostic representation alignment method, specifically targeting a federated multi-task learning scenario where users have arbitrary architectures and tasks. We will provide theorems and proofs in the context of Hogwild!, where each user's model executes full-batch SGD updates on its local data, with an arbitrary but fixed global model architecture. Derive a lower bound on the convergence rate, highlighting how dependencies among local representations constitute a key challenge. Consider theoretical results based on local Lipschitz conditions and sparse connectivity assumptions, as this links differing gradient updates in users to the expectation over instance representations, demonstrating orthogonality or similar approximations as regulation.

Consequently, forming privacy-friendly server-client architectures that minimize client-heterogeneity is conjectured to lead to substantial convergence improvements across users.

TITLE: Model-Agnostic Contrastive Loss with Weak Supervision for Federated Representation Learning

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient Federated Multi-Task Learning via Task Stealing and Subspace Projection
PROPOSAL: To reduce communication and computation overhead in federated multi-task learning, propose an efficient method called Task Stealing and Subspace Projection (TSSP). TSSP works by first selecting a "task owner" who stores the shared representation. Each participating user then shares their task-specific weights and the server trains the shared representation using a projected version of the received weights, which significantly reduces computation and communication costs for the server. Propose and evaluate several optimizers, such as the Projected Adagrad, its accelerated variants and consecutive multiplicative numerical schemes.
CONTROLS: Compare TSSP to existing communication-efficient methods for federated multi-task learning, such as federated distillation with product of experts compression
COST: 1440
PREDICTION: TSSP is expected to significantly reduce the communication and computation costs compared to baseline federated multi-task learning methods, while achieving comparable performance to the baseline. However, TSSP may introduce a slight degradation in performance due to the lossy projection and the overloading of information onto a single task owner.

TITLE: Evaluating Model-Agnostic Alignment for Federated Multi-Task Learning without Architectural Congruity
PROPOSAL: Experiment on the widely adopted FEMNIST and Shakespeare datasets used in federated multi-task learning benchmarks, where each user can have a different model architecture and task. Evaluate the performance of a model-agnostic alignment method based on a recently proposed geometric interpretation of kernel centered alignments, which ensures the alignment measure remains positive even for representations with different latent spaces. Additionally, incorporate a federated learning setup that supports model updates without exposing local iterations or gradients, to protect user privacy; a trade-off can be made for faster convergence and higher communication efficiency by allowing the server to receive only final model updates and feature statistics. Use a robust average of task-specific loss functions to accommodate the diversity of tasks and user policies.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: users are free to select their own architectures, with standard federated averaging.
Baseline 2: Architectural congruity with known heterogeneous architectures and semi-homogeneous task assignments.
COST: 1080
PREDICTION: We expect a 5-10 percent increase in collective accuracy for diverse users over standard federated averaging, with higher model diversity allowing for better representation convergence. However, adding users with significantly different tasks is expected to still cause a noticeable decrease in performance; conclusive results are best obtained when users are selected with moderate task compatibility, aside from personalization tasks.

Derive a lower bound on the convergence rate, highlighting how dependencies among local representations constitute a key challenge. Consider theoretical results based on local Lipschitz conditions and sparse connectivity assumptions, as this links differing gradient updates in users to the expectation over instance representations, demonstrating orthogonality or similar approximations as regulation.
CONTROLS: The Impact of Global Architecture Congruity on Convergence Speed

PREDICTION: With proofs of lower bounds, empirical convergence rates shall improve with restrictive conditions such as higher model sparsity or global architectural similarity. Consequently, forming privacy-friendly server-client architectures that minimize client-heterogeneity is conjectured to lead to substantial convergence improvements across users.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Task Architecture-Agnostic Federated Learning with Joint Representation Alignment
PROPOSAL: We design a novel federated multi-task learning method that leverages a robust and programmable architecture-agnostic contrastive learning mechanism to align the joint representations of multiple users' models. Specifically, we propose a task-agnostic framework that combines a pairwise cosine similarity between model representations and a symmetric autoencoder layer for reducing intra-task and inter-task discrepancies. This framework mitigates the need for model congruity, allowing users to utilize heterogeneous architectures and tasks.
CONTROLS: We provide baselines with the state-of-the-art methods in federated multi-task learning (e.g., federated distillation, knowledge-sharing methods), without model congruity, and their architecture-agnostic extensions. TITLE: Meta-Learning for Federated Multi-Task Learning with Adversarial Training
PROPOSAL: We explore meta-learning for federated multi-task learning, which involves leveraging the potential of a meta-model to rapidly adjust to various local tasks without significant retraining. PREDICTION: This approach is expected to demonstrate efficiency, distribution robustness, and task adaptability, and should be particularly beneficial in settings with non-homogeneous user models and a changing federated environment.

TITLE: Graph Neural Network-based Multi-Task Federated Learning with Hierarchical Knowledge Graph Construction
PROPOSAL: To improve the knowledge transfer efficiency and robustness in multi-task federated learning, we introduce a graph neural network (GNN)-based framework that leveraging hierarchical knowledge graph construction to model the complex relationships among tasks and users. Specifically, we build a layered knowledge graph to represent the task relationships, and feed it into a GNN to learn a shared representation for all tasks. However, the construction of the hierarchical knowledge graph may require significant computational resources and may not be scalable to extremely large task sets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Graph-based Knowledge Distillation in Federated Multi-task Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a graph-based knowledge distillation framework that enables knowledge transfer across users with heterogeneous model architectures and different tasks. In this framework, each user represents its model as a node in a graph, while the edges represent the similarity between the models. We then extend the InfoNCE loss to the graph setting and propose a graph-based contrastive loss that aligns the representations produced by all users simultaneously. This loss encourages the models to capture common task-agnostic information and learn from each other without sharing local data.
CONTROLS: tahun (ground truth without distillation), distilled (without graph-based framework), baseline InfoNCE loss (with pairwise alignment)
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: The proposed method can improve knowledge transfer and model generalization compared to existing methods, particularly in settings with complex task relationships. However, it may fail in cases where the graph structure is poorly initialized or the relationships between models are not accurately captured.

TITLE: Differential Privacy-Federated Multi-task Learning with Adaptive Noise Addition
PROPOSAL: We propose a differential privacy-preserving framework for federated multi-task learning that incorporates adaptive noise addition to protect user data. In this framework, the model adapts the amount of noise added to the user data based on the individual task complexities and user participation rates.
CONTROLS: same as before, plus evaluation on different differential privacy budgets
COST: 432000
PREDICTION: The proposed method can improve the privacy guarantees of federated multi-task learning while preserving the accuracy of the learned models. However, it may fail if the adaptive noise addition mechanism is not effective in balancing privacy and accuracy, or if the task complexities and user participation rates are highly variable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Federated Multi-task Learning Framework with Hierarchical Clustering and Knowledge Distillation
PROPOSAL: We propose a unified framework that combines hierarchical clustering and knowledge distillation for federated multi-task learning. In this framework, the model clusters similar tasks and users together, and uses knowledge distillation to transfer knowledge between tasks.
CONTROLS: same as before, plus evaluation on different clustering algorithms and knowledge distillation methods
COST: 72000
PREDICTION: The proposed method can improve the scalability and efficiency of federated multi-task learning by reducing the number of tasks and users to train on. However, it may fail if the hierarchical clustering algorithm is not effective in grouping similar tasks and users together, or if the knowledge distillation method is not effective in transferring knowledge between tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Graph-based Knowledge Distillation in Federated Multi-task Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a graph-based knowledge distillation framework that enables knowledge transfer across users with heterogeneous model architectures and different tasks. In this framework, each user represents its model as a node in a graph, while the edges represent the similarity between the models. We then extend the InfoNCE loss to the graph setting and propose a graph-based contrastive loss that aligns the representations produced by all users simultaneously. This loss encourages the models to capture common task-agnostic information and learn from each other without sharing local data.
CONTROLS: tahun (ground truth without distillation), distilled (without graph-based framework), baseline InfoNCE loss (with pairwise alignment)
COST: 36000
PREDICTION: The proposed method can improve knowledge transfer and model generalization compared to existing methods, particularly in settings with complex task relationships. However, it may fail in cases where the graph structure is poorly initialized or the relationships between models are not accurately captured.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED: Graph-based Knowledge Distillation in Federated Multi-task Learning
PROPOSAL: We revise the previous proposal to include a novel Graph Attention Network (GAT) for graph construction and a joint learning scheme for updating the model representations and the graph structure simultaneously. The GAT is used to learn the affinity matrix between models, while the joint learning scheme is designed to encourage models to focus on common patterns and learn from each other effectively.
CONTROLS: same as before, plus ablation study on GAT and joint learning scheme
COST: 54000
PREDICTION: The revised method can improve knowledge transfer and model generalization by capturing task relationships more accurately and learning from each other more effectively. However, it may still fail if the initialization of the graph structure is suboptimal or the number of users is very large, making the joint learning scheme computationally expensive.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Federated Multi-task Learning with Adversarial Graph Embeddings
PROPOSAL: We propose a framework that incorporates adversarial training to learn robust graph embeddings for federated multi-task learning. In this framework, a generator network learns to embed the graph structure, while a discriminator network tries to distinguish between the embedded graph and a noise vector. The generator and discriminator are trained simultaneously, and the generator's output is used to align the model representations.
CONTROLS: same as before, plus baseline with vanilla graph embeddings
COST: 81000
PREDICTION: The proposed method can improve knowledge transfer and model generalization by learning robust graph embeddings that are less affected by outliers and noisy data. However, it may fail if the generator and discriminator are not carefully balanced, or if the graph structure is too complex.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Federated Multi-task Learning with Domain-Adversarial Regularization
PROPOSAL: We propose a framework that incorporates domain-adversarial regularization to learn task-agnostic representations that are invariant to different task domains. In this framework, a domain classifier is trained to predict the task domain from the model representations, and the task classifier is updated to learn task-agnostic representations that confuse the domain classifier.
CONTROLS: same as before, plus baseline with vanilla task alignment
COST: 72000
PREDICTION: The proposed method can improve knowledge transfer and model generalization by learning task-agnostic representations that capture common patterns across different task domains. However, it may fail if the domain classifier is too powerful and overshadows the task classifier, or if the task domains are too dissimilar.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED: Federated Multi-task Learning with Domain-Adversarial Regularization
PROPOSAL NUMBER: 3
REVISION: We revise the previous proposal to include a novel meta-learning approach that learns to adapt the domain-adversarial regularization for different task domains. In this revised framework, the model learns to select the most relevant domain-adversarial regularization term for each task domain, and updates the model representations accordingly.
CONTROLS: same as before, plus ablation study on meta-learning approach and analysis of regularization term selection
COST: 108000
PREDICTION: The revised method can improve knowledge transfer and model generalization by adapting the domain-adversarial regularization for different task domains, and learning more robust and generalizable representations. However, it may still fail if the meta-learning approach is not properly balanced or if the task domains are too diverse.

PROPOSAL: We propose a sparse attention mechanism that allows the model to focus on a subset of the overall set of tasks and users, while still capturing the relationships between tasks and users. This approach can lead to a significant reduction in computational cost and improve the overall efficiency of the federated learning process.

PREDICTION: The proposed method can improve the efficiency of the federated learning process and reduce the computational cost. However, it may fail if the sparse attention mechanism is not effective in capturing the relationships between tasks and users, or if the task graph is too dense.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Federated Multi-Task Learning via Joint Representation Alignment
PROPOSAL: Implement a federated multi-task learning method that combines knowledge distillation with a novel Gramian-based loss, designed to align representations from multiple users with heterogeneous architectures. This method, dubbed "FedAlign", involves each user fine-tuning a pre-trained foundation model on their local task, then distilling their knowledge to a central model. The central model, after collecting representations from all users, computes a common representation space using a Gramian-based contrastive loss.
CONTROLS:  Compare FedAlign with existing approaches on several benchmarks, including personalization-based methods (FedProg, FedMatch) and multi-task methods (FEDMD, PQ-MF); also compare FedAlign to a baseline that uses InfoNCE loss on every pair of models.
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: FedAlign should outperform existing methods in terms of generalization performance, while maintaining a communication overhead comparable to InfoNCE-based approaches; however, it may struggle on datasets with extremely diverse representation spaces, leading to reduced alignment quality.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Improving FedAlign with Asynchronous Update of the Central Model
PROPOSAL: Update the central model in FedAlign asynchronously to reduce communication overhead and improve convergence. Each user still fine-tunes their pre-trained foundation model and distills the knowledge to the central model. However, new users can start participating in the federated learning process without requiring immediate updates to the central model. This can be achieved through an aggregation protocol, such as those proposed in SCAFFOLD or FedPAQ, which allow for efficient and decentralized aggregation of(model) updates.
CONTROLS: Compare to the baseline FedAlign with synchronous central model updates, as well as to existing methods that exploit asynchronous aggregation (FEDPAQ, SCAFFOLD) in non-federated settings.
COST: 5332.8
PREDICTION: Asynchronous update of the central model will significantly reduce the communication overhead and improve the overall convergence rate of FedAlign, making it practical for large-scale applications; however, this update approach may introduce additional latency, compromising the overall speed of training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Modal Representation Alignment via Heterogeneous Embedding Alignment
PROPOSAL: Extend FedAlign to support multi-modal federated learning by incorporating heterogeneous embedding alignment. Each user is associated with a unique modality (text, image, audio, etc.) and a respective representation space. A new alignment loss is introduced to bring the representations of different modalities into a common space. This is achieved through a graph neural network that models the relationships between modalities and their corresponding embeddings.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the performance of the proposed multi-modal extension on benchmark datasets from diverse modalities (text: 20 Newsgroups, image: CIFAR-10, audio: UrbanSound8K).
COST: 7344
PREDICTION: The proposed multi-modal extension can effectively align representations across diverse modalities and improve overall model performance. However, modular complexity increases which can du during discrepancy reduction.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Heterogeneous Embedding Alignment with Domain-Adversarial Training
PROPOSAL: Improve the heterogeneous embedding alignment in the multi-modal extension by introducing a domain-adversarial training (DAT) component. This involves training the graph neural network to not only align the representations across modalities but also to learn invariant features that are robust to domain shifts. DAT is achieved by adding domain-specific classification heads to the network, which are trained to predict the source domain of each sample.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of the DAT-enhanced multi-modal extension with the original heterogenous embedding alignment on benchmark datasets with domain shifts (e.g., ImageNet-A).
COST: 8649
PREDICTION: The addition of DAT will improve the robustness of the aligned representations to domain shifts and reduce the performance degradation when transferring knowledge across modalities. However, DAT may increase the risk of overfitting if not carefully regularized.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robustness of FedAlign to Model Poisoning Attacks
PROPOSAL: Investigate the robustness of FedAlign to model poisoning attacks, which are a common threat in federated learning settings. We propose to add a defense mechanism that detects and mitigates model poisoning attacks through a novel signature-based approach. This approach identifies and aggregates samples that contain malicious labels or updates, effectively reducing the influence of such samples on the central model.
CONTROLS: Compare the robustness of FedAlign with the proposed defense mechanism to existing methods (e.g., ADMM, CDART) on benchmarks with model poisoning attacks (e.g., Paraprtrust).
COST: 10680
PREDICTION: The proposed defense mechanism effectively detects and mitigates model poisoning attacks, improving the robustness of FedAlign. However, it may incur additional computation and communication overhead, compromising training efficiency.

TITLE: Adaptive Knowledge Transfer via Selective Distillation
PROPOSAL: Enhance FedAlign by introducing an adaptive knowledge transfer mechanism through selective distillation. This involves dynamically selecting the knowledge to be transferred from the users to the central model based on their task-specific performance. The central model adapts to the changing knowledge landscape, focusing on the most relevant information to improve overall performance.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of FedAlign with the adaptive knowledge transfer mechanism to existing methods on benchmarks (e.g., ImageNet, CIFAR-10) with diverse task spaces and changing knowledge landscapes.
COST: 12600
PREDICTION: The adaptive knowledge transfer mechanism improves the performance of FedAlign by selectively focusing on the most relevant information. However, it may incur additional computation and training overhead, which may slow down the convergence of the central model.

TITLE: Exploiting Long-term Consequences of Noisy Label Correction through Episodic Training
PROPOSAL: Train a deep neural network on a noisy dataset using episodic training, where the network is periodically reinitialized and trained on a newly sampled subset of the noisy dataset. This approach aims to simulate the long-term consequences of label correction decisions by iteratively refining the network's parameters based on the corrected labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal-Dynamic Label Noise Modeling with Graph Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel method to model label noise as a temporal-dynamic process, where the noise patterns change over time. We use a graph neural network (GNN) to learn the dynamics of the label noise, where the nodes represent the samples and the edges represent the similarity between them. By integrating the GNN with our active learning framework, we can selectively correct noisy labels based on the predicted noise distribution. We evaluate our method on datasets with strong temporal correlations in label noise and demonstrate its effectiveness in reducing the impact of noise.
CONTROLS: We compare our method against state-of-the-art active learning approaches and a baseline GNN-based model without the temporal-dynamic label noise modeling.
COST: 2500 GPU-hours 
PREDICTION: By accounting for the temporal-dynamic aspect of label noise, our method can adapt to changing noise patterns and improve the accuracy of noisy samples, leading to better overall performance on real-world datasets.

TITLE: Jointly Learning from Noisy Labels and Synthetic Data
PROPOSAL: We propose an approach that leverages both real-world noisy labeled data and synthetic data to improve the robustness of deep neural networks. Our method learns a shared representation between the noisy labeled samples and synthetic samples, and then adapts this representation to make predictions on the clean test data. We use a recently proposed synthetic dataset generator that can produce high-quality synthetic images with varying intensity and noise levels, mimicking real-world data. This allows us to augment our training data with diverse examples and further enhance the model's generalization ability.
CONTROLS: We compare our method against state-of-the-art approaches that only utilize real-world noisy labeled data or synthetic data separately, as well as a baseline that combines both but without the joint learning framework.
COST: 4000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By judiciously combining noisy labeled data and synthetic data, our method can effectively reduce the adverse effects of noisy labels, achieve improved generalization performance, and maintain robustness under diverse scenarios.

TITLE: Temporal-Dynamic Label Noise Modeling with Enhanced Graph Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: We refine our Temporal-Dynamic Label Noise Modeling with Graph Neural Networks method to better capture the complex relationships between the label noise patterns and the input features. We introduce a conditional dependency between the graph structure and the label noise, allowing the model to adaptively select the most relevant edges for the specific label noise scenario. This conditional dependency is learned using a novel graph attention mechanism that views the label noise as a changing, conditional distribution over the edges. Additionally, we enhance the loss function by incorporating a contrastive term that encourages the model to recognize similarities and differences among the label noise patterns.
CONTROLS: We compare the updated approach against both the original Temporal-Dynamic Label Noise Modeling with Graph Neural Networks and a state-of-the-art graph-based approach that lacks the conditional dependency and the contrastive term.
COST: 8400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By incorporating a conditional dependency between the graph structure and the label noise, and a contrastive term to the loss function, our updated method can more effectively capture the compound effects of the label noise and learn a more accurate noise model.

TITLE: Temporal-Dynamic Label Noise Modeling with Graph Neural Networks
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel method to model label noise as a temporal-dynamic process, where the noise patterns change over time. We use a graph neural network (GNN) to learn the dynamics of the label noise, where the nodes represent the samples and the edges represent the similarity between them. By integrating the GNN with our active learning framework, we can selectively correct noisy labels based on the predicted noise distribution. We evaluate our method on datasets with strong temporal correlations in label noise and demonstrate its effectiveness in reducing the impact of noise.
CONTROLS: We compare our method against state-of-the-art active learning approaches and a baseline GNN-based model without the temporal-dynamic label noise modeling.

This allows us to augment our training data with diverse examples and further enhance the model's generalization ability.

PROPOSAL: We will investigate the use of context-aware label filtering, where the filtration process is informed by the instance features and the model's predictions. COST: 9600
PREDICTION: We expect a significant improvement in performance over the baseline, particularly for datasets where the instance-dependent noise is prominent, due to our contextual filtration strategy. However, our method may struggle in scenarios where the noise is highly correlated across instances.

Starting from an initial training process on noisily labeled datasets (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and MissingLabel1M), we will iteratively select samples to correct and retrain the model until convergence or CPU time limits.

However, human annotation costs and exploration-exploitation trade-offs in uncertainty-driven sampling strategies might compromise performance in resource-constrained settings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Robust Loss Functions for Noisy Labels
PROPOSAL: We propose a family of uncertainty-aware robust loss functions that combine the advantages of standard cross-entropy loss with the knowledge of the model's predictive uncertainty. To accommodate noisy labels, we exploit the difference between two predictive probability distributions: the standard predictive probability q(x) for a clean label and the noisy predictive probability p(x) for a corrupted label. We then define the robust loss function as a weighted sum of the standard cross-entropy loss and a complementary uncertainty-based penalty term. This combined loss encourages the model to be robust against noisy labels by focusing on the uncertainty of its predictions.
CONTROLS: We compare our proposed loss function against standard cross-entropy loss and state-of-the-art robust loss functions, such as the mean teacher and co-teaching approach.
COST: 19200
PREDICTION: The proposed loss function is expected to achieve at least a 5% improvement in test accuracy over standard cross-entropy loss on noisy datasets and up to a 10% improvement over robust loss functions under noisy high-noise scenarios without the risk of overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Robust Label Correction through Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL: We will adapt a meta-learning approach to develop a label correction model that can learn to correct noisy labels based on the model's past correction experiences. Specifically, we will use a model-agnostic meta-learning (MAML) algorithm to learn a generalizable correction model that can be fine-tuned for different tasks and datasets. We will evaluate the performance of our approach on several real-world datasets, including Clothing1M, WebVision, and Nigerian 200.
CONTROLS: We will compare our approach with state-of-the-art label correction methods, including Co-teaching, MentorNet, and Gemini, as well as a strong baseline that uses a pre-trained model with a robust loss function.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our approach should significantly improve the accuracy of label correction, especially in complex and noisy scenarios. However, the meta-learning algorithm may struggle to generalize to unseen datasets, and the approach may require careful hyperparameter tuning to achieve the best results.

Note: This proposal sets the stage for a set of experiments that will evaluate the effectiveness of meta-learning for label correction. We will revise or add subsequent proposals to explore specific aspects of this approach and compare it with alternative strategies.

However, the meta-learning algorithm may struggle to generalize to unseen datasets, and the approach may require careful hyperparameter tuning to achieve the best results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Iterative RGB-Event Fusion with Multi-Resolution Analysis
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of iterative RGB-event fusion methods on dynamic scenes, incorporating multi-resolution analysis to capture varying spatial frequencies. We'll implement a custom fusion layer that takes the current RGB frame $I_t$, the event stream $\mathcal{E}_{t-\Delta t \to t+\delta t}$, and previous fusion outputs as input to predict the segmentation mask at $t+\delta t$. We will use a combination of U-Net architecture and the dilated version of ResNet-50 (with several dilation rates) to extract features of varying scales and resolutions.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Event-only semantic segmentation with standard U-Net; Baseline 2: RGB-only semantic segmentation with the standard U-Net; Baseline 3: State-of-the-art multi-modal RGB-event fusion methods on dynamic scenes.
COST: 3176 GPU hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement over baseline event-only segmentation by 10-15% and better adaptation to dynamic scenes, but our method may struggle with high-frequency motions due to its multi-resolution approach.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Top-Down Guidance for RGB-Event Fusion with Temporal Attention
PROPOSAL: Develop a top-down guidance network that takes the predicted segmentation masks from the iterative RGB-event fusion method (Proposal 1) as input, and provides spatial attention to the event stream to selectively emphasize relevant information. This attention mechanism, combined with a temporal convolutional network, enables the capture of long-range temporal dependencies between events. We'll add a self-attention-based temporal module that encourages the network to attend to events more relevant to predicting the semantic map at $t+\delta t$.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1 (from Proposal 1); Ablation Study 1: RGB-event fusion without top-down guidance; Ablation Study 2: No attention mechanism in the top-down guidance network.
COST: 4400 GPU hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement over baseline 1 by 15-20% in accuracy, as our method enhances the ability of the model to capture temporal dynamics and spatial dependencies. However, dependency on early predictions in Proposal 1 might limit the performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Unguided Event Temporal Encoding (EUte)
PROPOSAL: Pose an alternative approach by directly modeling the temporal structure of the event stream without the RGB frame's guidance. This method utilizes continuous-time Bayesian neural networks to denote events as temporal intervals with spike times, allowing for effective modeling of temporal relationships. We will compare the two methods using different distance metrics.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1 (from Proposal 1); EUte with convolutional neural networks, EUte without convolutional neural networks, Baseline 2: RGB-only segmentation at high frame rates.
COST: 5500 GPU hours
PREDICTION: EUte is predicted to underperform Proposal 2 due to its simplicity and limited capacity to utilize individual event information, but may be more efficient in processing long, unstructured event streams, potentially outperforming baseline 2 under those circumstances.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Integrating RGB-Event Fusion with 3D Spatiotemporal Context
PROPOSAL: Incorporate a 3D convolutional neural network component to learn long-range spatiotemporal context from both RGB frames and event streams. Utilizing a space-time volume constructed from consecutive RGB frames and event clusters, this approach enables a richer understanding of scenes and facilitates robust predictions across multiple time steps. We'll focus on capturing static scene features from RGB frames and emphasize transient event data from event streams.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1 (from Revised Proposal 1); Baseline 2: RGB-only segmentation at high frame rates; Ablation Study 1: No 3D convolutional neural network component; Ablation Study 2: Space-time volume is constructed using only event clusters.
COST: 6300 GPU hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement over baseline 1 by 25-30% due to its enhanced ability to leverage both short-term and long-term spatiotemporal patterns. However, it might be sensitive to scene clutter and temporal noise in the event streams.

TITLE: Novel Scene Understanding with Probabilistic Temporal Transformations
PROPOSAL: Model the uncertainty of scene transformations across time using probabilistic temporal transformations (PTT). PTT combines generative adversarial networks (GANs) with a Markov chain theory to simulate future events based on the initial RGB frame and event stream. This enables predictions at arbitrary time steps, particularly in highly dynamic scenes.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1 (from Revised Proposal 1); Baseline 2: Event-only segmentation with GANs; Baseline 3: RGB-only segmentation at high frame rates; Ablation Study 1: No GAN component in PTT; Ablation Study 2: Only Markov chain modeling.
COST: 7432 GPU hours
PREDICTION: PTT is predicted to outperform baseline 1 by 35-40% due to its representation of temporal uncertainty, but it might be prone to mode collapse and may require large datasets for effective training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Iterative RGB-Event Fusion with Multi-Resolution Analysis
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of iterative RGB-event fusion methods on dynamic scenes, incorporating multi-resolution analysis to capture varying spatial frequencies. We'll implement a custom fusion layer that takes the current RGB frame $I_t$, the event stream $\mathcal{E}_{t-\Delta t \to t+\delta t}$, and previous fusion outputs as input to predict the segmentation mask at $t+\delta t$. We will use a combination of U-Net architecture and the dilated version of ResNet-50 (with several dilation rates) to extract features of varying scales and resolutions.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Event-only semantic segmentation with standard U-Net; Baseline 2: RGB-only semantic segmentation with the standard U-Net; Baseline 3: State-of-the-art multi-modal RGB-event fusion methods on dynamic scenes.
COST: 9500 GPU hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement over baseline event-only segmentation by 10-15% and better adaptation to dynamic scenes, but our method may struggle with high-frequency motions due to its multi-resolution approach.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Top-Down Guidance for RGB-Event Fusion with Temporal Attention
PROPOSAL: Develop a top-down guidance network that takes the predicted segmentation masks from the iterative RGB-event fusion method (Proposal 1) as input, and provides spatial attention to the event stream to selectively emphasize relevant information. This attention mechanism, combined with a temporal convolutional network, enables the capture of long-range temporal dependencies between events. We'll add a self-attention-based temporal module that encourages the network to attend to events more relevant to predicting the semantic map at $t+\delta t$.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1 (from Proposal 1); Ablation Study 1: RGB-event fusion without top-down guidance; Ablation Study 2: No attention mechanism in the top-down guidance network.
COST: 13200 GPU hours
PREDICTION: Expected improvement over baseline 1 by 15-20% in accuracy, as our method enhances the ability of the model to capture temporal dynamics and spatial dependencies. However, dependency on early predictions in Proposal 1 might limit the performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Unguided Event Temporal Encoding (EUte)
PROPOSAL: Pose an alternative approach by directly modeling the temporal structure of the event stream without the RGB frame's guidance. This method utilizes continuous-time Bayesian neural networks to denote events as temporal intervals with spike times, allowing for effective modeling of temporal relationships. We will compare the two methods using different distance metrics.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1 (from Proposal 1); EUte with convolutional neural networks, EUte without convolutional neural networks, Baseline 2: RGB-only segmentation at high frame rates.
COST: 16500 GPU hours
PREDICTION: EUte is predicted to underperform Proposal 2 due to its simplicity and limited capacity to utilize individual event information, but may be more efficient in processing long, unstructured event streams, potentially outperforming baseline 2 under those circumstances.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Revised Evaluating Iterative RGB-Event Fusion with Multi-Resolution Analysis
PROPOSAL: Modify Proposal 1 by incorporating another major component into the architecture. On top of multi-resolution analysis and iterative fusion with standard U-Net, we incorporate a novel module to insert probability distributions for temporal interpolation from the output convolutional layers to act as multi-class averaging factors in unseen time slots. This can more effectively capture illusory foreground information and reduce temporal ambiguities.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1 (adjusts Proposal 1 with ablation study on new redistribution factor); Ablation Study 1: RGB-event fusion with the new temporal redistribution factor; Ablation Study 2: No temporal redistribution factor, including only spatial analysis.
COST: 10500 GPU hours
PREDICTION: The model with temporal redistribution factors is expected to manifest a 10-15% enhanced performance over its original counterpart in various autonomous driving scenarios and to achieve better correlates in negative counterparts doubtful situations.
