ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temporal Event-Driven Attention Network
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel Temporal Event-Driven Attention Network (TEDAN) to predict dense semantic maps at arbitrary timestamps within the perceptual gap between low-frame-rate frames. TEDAN aggregates event streams using a temporal attention mechanism, focusing on the most relevant events and weights them based on their temporal proximity to the prediction target. The weighted event embedding is then fused with the initial RGB frame using a dual attention gate, selectively highlighting informative regions in the RGB image. The fused features are fed into a lightweight, encoder-decoder architecture that generates the predicted semantic map. Our approach is designed to capture the high-temporal-resolution motion information from the event stream while leveraging the spatial context from the RGB frame.
CONTROLS: We compare TEDAN to a naive event-driven approach that uses the event stream as input without fusion and to a state-of-the-art RGB video semantic segmentation method adapted forOne-Stage Open Gan Network baseline ONet-GAN Baseline), as well as to recent fusion-based methods that lack causal and anytime prediction capabilities.
COST: 1000
PREDICTION: We expect TEDAN to outperform the naive event-driven approach and to achieve competitive performance with the adapted state-of-the-art RGB method on the KITTI-odom dataset, especially in Highly dynamic scenes. While TEDAN is generally robust to high velocities, its performance might degrade in extremely long prediction intervals where object movement/occlusion might be severe.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event-Driven Multi-Modal Fusion with Causal Attention
PROPOSAL: We propose an Event-Driven Multi-Modal Fusion with Causal Attention (EDMFA) network that leverages the event stream to provide context-aware, causal guidance for selecting relevant regions in the RGB frame. EDMFA employs a causal attention mechanism that learns to focus on regions in the RGB image that correspond to upcoming events in the event stream, thus preventing the network from attending to regions that would be occluded or have moved by the time the prediction is made. The weighted RGB features are then fused with the weighted event embedding using a multi-modal fusion module, generating the predicted semantic map. Our approach ensures both causal and anytime prediction capabilities while capturing the complex relationships between the event stream, RGB image, and the semantics of the scene.
CONTROLS: We compare EDMFA to TEDAN, the naive event-driven approach, and the adapted RGB video semantic segmentation method (ONet-GAN Baseline), as well as to recent fusion-based methods.
COST: 1086.45289
PREDICTION: We expect EDMFA to outperform the naive event-driven approach and to achieve competitive performance with TEDAN and the adapted RGB method on the nuScenes dataset, with improved handling of occlusion and object movement due to its causal attention mechanism. While EDMFA might be computationally more expensive than TEDAN, its performance might degrade in scenarios with very high velocities and long prediction intervals.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Event-Driven RGB Fusion
PROPOSAL: We propose a Hierarchical Event-Driven RGB Fusion (HEDRF) framework to predict dense semantic maps within the perceptual gap between low-frame-rate frames. HEDRF employs a coarse-to-fine fusion strategy, where the event stream is first processed by a high-level fusion module to generate a sparse, high-level semantic map. This map is then used as a prior to guide a low-level fusion module that focuses on refining the semantics of specific regions in the RGB image, leveraging the event stream's high temporal resolution. Our approach is designed to effectively capture both the high-level semantics and the fine-grained details in the scene, while ensuring causal and anytime prediction capabilities.
CONTROLS: We compare HEDRF to TEDAN, EDMFA, the naive event-driven approach, and the adapted RGB video semantic segmentation method (ONet-GAN Baseline), as well as to recent fusion-based methods.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: We expect HEDRF to outperform TEDAN and EDMFA by better capturing the high-level semantics and fine-grained details in the scene, especially in complex scenarios with multiple objects and occlusions. While HEDRF might suffer from increased computational overhead, its performance might degrade in scenarios with extremely long prediction intervals and very high velocities.

TITLE: Real-World Event Camera Calibration and Dataset
PROPOSAL: To evaluate the performance of the proposed methods in realistic settings, we create a new dataset, "Real-World Event Scenes" (RWES), consisting of event camera recordings from various scenarios such as busy streets, construction sites, and back alleys. We also develop a calibration pipeline to adjust for non-uniformity and non-linearity in the event cameras. This enables us to generate high-quality, ground-truth semantic maps to train and validate our methods.
CONTROLS: RWES will be used as the primary evaluation dataset for the proposed methods, with optional benchmarks against other event camera datasets such as DVS-128 and DAVIS.
COST: 1536
PREDICTION: We expect RWES to become a valuable benchmark for event camera-based perception in real-world scenarios, highlighting the importance of calibrating event cameras for accurate semantic mapping tasks in various conditions. However, the complexity of real-world scenes might introduce new challenges, and the effectiveness of our proposed methods may vary depending on the specific scene characteristics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dilation-Factor Based Encoder for Event-Driven Images
PROPOSAL: To better capture the intricate patterns and temporal relationships in event-driven images, we propose a novel dilation-factor based encoder (DFE). DFE adaptively adjusts the filter receptive fields based on the dilation factor, allowing for both fine-grained and coarse-grained feature extraction. This enables the network to capture both small and large-scale features in the event-driven images, leading to improved event-camera-based perception performance. We incorporate DFE into the Hierarchical Event-Driven RGB Fusion (HEDRF) framework to enhance its performance.
CONTROLS: We compare DFE-enhanced HEDRF to original HEDRF, TEDAN, EDMFA, and other state-of-the-art methods.
COST: 1665.1
PREDICTION: We expect DFE-enhanced HEDRF to show significant performance improvements, especially in scenarios with complex occlusion and scene diversity. However, the increased complexity of the network may lead to higher computational demands.

PROPOSAL: We propose a Graph Attention-Based Multi-Frame Fusion (GAMFF) approach for event cameras, which leverages a graph attention network to selectively aggregate event-driven features from multiple frames in the temporal vicinity of the target prediction timestamp. GAMFF is designed to capture complex relationships between events across different frames, enabling robust and accurate predictions even in scenarios with rapid scene changes or object movements. We integrate GAMFF into the HEDRF framework to further enhance its performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: One-Shot Training for Event Camera-Based Perception
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel one-shot training approach for event camera-based perception methods, which enables us to train a single model on a small set of example scenes and generalize it to unseen environments. Our one-shot learning approach utilizes a combination of metric learning and knowledge distillation, allowing the model to learn a shared representation across different scenes and adapt to new environments with minimal fine-tuning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our one-shot training approach on various event camera-based perception tasks.
CONTROLS: We compare our one-shot training approach to traditional multi-shot training on various benchmarks and demonstrate its ability to generalize across different scenes.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: We expect our one-shot training approach to significantly reduce training time and improve generalization across different scenes, enabling more efficient and adaptive event camera-based perception systems. However, the effectiveness of our approach may depend on the quality of the initial training data and the ability of the model to extract robust and transferable features from the event stream.

CONTROLS: We compare HEDRF to TEDAN, EDMFA, the naive event-driven approach, and the adapted RGB video semantic segmentation method (ONet-GAN Baseline), as well as to recent fusion-based methods.
COST: 3575
PREDICTION: We expect HEDRF to outperform TEDAN and EDMFA by better capturing the high-level semantics and fine-grained details in the scene, especially in complex scenarios with multiple objects and occlusions. While HEDRF might suffer from increased computational overhead, its performance might degrade in scenarios with extremely long prediction intervals and very high velocities.

ACTION: REVISE | Number: 2
TITLE: Event-Driven Multi-Modal Fusion with Causal Attention
REVISED PROPOSAL: In the revised version of the EDMFA network, we incorporate an additional module that learns to predict the probability distribution over possible semantic segmentations within the perceptual gap between frames. This probability distribution is then used to guide the causal attention mechanism, allowing the network to adaptively focus on regions in the RGB image that are most likely to be relevant to the upcoming events in the event stream. This adaptability is crucial in complex scenarios where the uncertainty in the event stream is high, and the true semantic segmentation is ambiguous.
CONTROLS: The comparison remains the same as before.
COST: 3875
PREDICTION: We expect the revised EDMFA to outperform the original version by adaptively focusing on the most relevant regions in the RGB image, especially in scenarios with high uncertainty in the event stream. While the revised EDMFA might suffer from increased model complexity, its performance might degrade in scenarios with extremely long prediction intervals and very high velocities, where the uncertainty in the event stream becomes overwhelming.

ACTION: REVISE | Number: 2
TITLE: Event-Driven Multi-Modal Fusion with Causal Attention
REVISED PROPOSAL: In the revised version of EDMFA, we use a Learned Event Gate (LEG) that selectively filters out irrelevant or noisy events in the event stream. The LEG is trained jointly with the causal attention mechanism to learn a policy that decides which events to include or discard based on their predicted impact on the final semantic map. This addition aims to improve the robustness of EDMFA to noisy or abnormal events, common in real-world scenarios.
CONTROLS: We compare the revised EDMFA to the original version, as well as to TEDAN, EDMFA, the naive event-driven approach, and the adapted RGB video semantic segmentation method (ONet-GAN Baseline), and recent fusion-based methods.
COST: 4125
PREDICTION: We expect the revised EDMFA to show improved robustness to noisy or abnormal events in the event stream, leading to enhanced overall performance in challenging scenarios with irregular motion or sensor noise. However, the LEG module might introduce additional complexity and computational overhead.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Event Camera Calibration and Dataset
PROPOSAL: To evaluate the performance of the proposed methods in realistic settings, we create a new dataset, "Real-World Event Scenes" (RWES), consisting of event camera recordings from various scenarios such as busy streets, construction sites, and back alleys. We also develop a calibration pipeline to adjust for non-uniformity and non-linearity in the event cameras. This enables us to generate high-quality, ground-truth semantic maps to train and validate our methods.
CONTROLS: RWES will be used as the primary evaluation dataset for the proposed methods, with optional benchmarks against other event camera datasets such as DVS-128 and DAVIS.
COST: 4600
PREDICTION: We expect RWES to become a valuable benchmark for event camera-based perception in real-world scenarios, highlighting the importance of calibrating event cameras for accurate semantic mapping tasks in various conditions. However, the complexity of real-world scenes might introduce new challenges, and the effectiveness of our proposed methods may vary depending on the specific scene characteristics.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dilation-Factor Based Encoder for Event-Driven Images
PROPOSAL: To better capture the intricate patterns and temporal relationships in event-driven images, we propose a novel dilation-factor based encoder (DFE). DFE adaptively adjusts the filter receptive fields based on the dilation factor, allowing for both fine-grained and coarse-grained feature extraction. This enables the network to capture both small and large-scale features in the event-driven images, leading to improved event-camera-based perception performance. We incorporate DFE into the Hierarchical Event-Driven RGB Fusion (HEDRF) framework to enhance its performance.
CONTROLS: We compare DFE-enhanced HEDRF to original HEDRF, TEDAN, EDMFA, and other state-of-the-art methods.
COST: 4975
PREDICTION: We expect DFE-enhanced HEDRF to show significant performance improvements, especially in scenarios with complex occlusion and scene diversity. However, the increased complexity of the network may lead to higher computational demands.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Graph Attention-Based Multi-Frame Fusion for Event Cameras
PROPOSAL: We propose a Graph Attention-Based Multi-Frame Fusion (GAMFF) approach for event cameras, which leverages a graph attention network to selectively aggregate event-driven features from multiple frames in the temporal vicinity of the target prediction timestamp. GAMFF is designed to capture complex relationships between events across different frames, enabling robust and accurate predictions even in scenarios with rapid scene changes or object movements. We integrate GAMFF into the HEDRF framework to further enhance its performance.
CONTROLS: We compare GAMFF-enhanced HEDRF to original HEDRF, TEDAN, EDMFA, and other state-of-the-art methods on various benchmarks.
COST: 5250
PREDICTION: We expect GAMFF-enhanced HEDRF to exhibit improved performance in scenarios with complex temporal relationships and rapid scene changes, such as busy intersections or crowded areas. However, the computational complexity of GAMFF might lead to performance degradation in low-power or resource-constrained devices.

ACTION: REVISE | Number: 5
TITLE: Dilation-Factor Based Encoder for Event-Driven Images
REVISED PROPOSAL: In the revised version of the Dilation-Factor Based Encoder (DFE), we incorporate a hierarchical feature pyramid structure to enhance its ability to capture features at multiple scales. This allows DFE to better handle complex scenes with varying densities of events and stimuli, such as those encountered in autonomous driving or drone navigation scenarios. We also integrate a progressive feature fusion mechanism that adaptively blends features from multiple scales, further improving the robustness of DFE.
CONTROLS: We compare the revised DFE-enhanced HEDRF to original HEDRF, TEDAN, EDMFA, and other state-of-the-art methods on various benchmarks.
COST: 5525
PREDICTION: We expect the revised DFE-enhanced HEDRF to exhibit improved performance in complex scenarios with varying densities of events, such as busy urban areas or areas with heavy construction, and demonstrate robustness to changing environments and stimuli. However, the increased complexity of the revised DFE might lead to higher computational demands and memory usage.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: One-Shot Training for Event Camera-Based Perception
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel one-shot training approach for event camera-based perception methods, which enables us to train a single model on a small set of example scenes and generalize it to unseen environments. Our one-shot learning approach utilizes a combination of metric learning and knowledge distillation, allowing the model to learn a shared representation across different scenes and adapt to new environments with minimal fine-tuning. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our one-shot training approach on various event camera-based perception tasks.
CONTROLS: We compare our one-shot training approach to traditional multi-shot training on various benchmarks and demonstrate its ability to generalize across different scenes.
COST: 6000
PREDICTION: We expect our one-shot training approach to significantly reduce training time and improve generalization across different scenes, enabling more efficient and adaptive event camera-based perception systems. However, the effectiveness of our approach may depend on the quality of the initial training data and the ability of the model to extract robust and transferable features from the event stream.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: RGB-Event Fusion with Spatial Attention
PROPOSAL: Develop a new model architecture that combines a recurrent neural network (RNN) with a spatial attention mechanism to effectively merge the static semantic context of a single past RGB frame with the temporally dense event stream. The RNN encodes the event stream, and the attention mechanism highlights the most important event regions that correspond to the RGB frame. We use a U-Net as the backbone for the RGB encoder.
CONTROLS: (1) A fusion model without spatial attention, (2) A standard MRCNN model on the event stream alone
COST: 332.2
PREDICTION: The model with spatial attention should outperform the model without attention by at least 5% in terms of IoU, and also outperform the MRCNN model with a difference of at least 2% in IoU. The model might struggle with scenes having many objects or complex spatial relationships between them, which could lead to a 2-3% degradation in performance.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: TemporalReasoning Module for Predictive Segmentation
PROPOSAL: Design a TemporalReasoning module that takes the event stream and produces a probability distribution over possible locations and types of objects within the scene, given the RGB frame as context. This module will reason over the event sequence to infer the probability of different objects being present at the target timestamp, and produce a set of potential object hypotheses. These object hypotheses will then be passed through a classifier to obtain the final segmentation.
CONTROLS: (1) RGB-Event Fusion with Spatial Attention from Proposal 1, (2) A baseline model that simply extrapolates the segmentation from the initial RGB frame
COST: 500
PREDICTION: The TemporalReasoning module should improve the performance of the RGB-Event Fusion with Spatial Attention model by at least 3% in terms of IoU, especially in scenes with high object motion or occlusions. However, it may also introduce some noise in the object hypotheses due to the inherent uncertainty in event-based sensing, which could lead to a 1-2% degradation in performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Harnessing RGB-Event Consistency via Pseudo-Labels
PROPOSAL: Propose an unsupervised learning technique that generates pseudo-labels for the event stream by predicting the segmentation from the RGB frame, and then use these pseudo-labels to train the TemporalReasoning module. This pseudo-label generation process would encourage the TemporalReasoning module to be consistent with the RGB frame, while also leveraging the fine-grained temporal information from the event stream.
CONTROLS: (1) TemporalReasoning Module for Predictive Segmentation with random initialization, (2) RGB-Event Fusion with Spatial Attention
COST: 665.042
PREDICTION: The pseudo-labeling technique should improve the performance of the TemporalReasoning module by at least 5% in terms of IoU, by effectively aligning the RGB and event modalities. However, the quality of the pseudo-labels may degrade over time, especially in dynamic scenes, which could lead to a 2-3% degradation in performance if not properly regularized.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Fusing Static and Dynamic Information with Event-Driven Expert Attention
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel rgb-event fusion model that leverages event-driven expert attention to focus on the most informative events for predicting dense semantic segmentation maps at arbitrary timestamps. The model consists of two branches: a traditional CNN-based RGB encoder and an event-driven encoder that aggregates and focuses on the most relevant events.
Utilizing the attentions learned by the event-driven encoder, we can dynamically utilize information from both the RGB and event streams. This allows the model to selectively emphasize emerging or disappearing objects, adapting to the dynamic nature of the scene. To train our model, we will use the Cityscapes, KITTI Vision, and nuScenes datasets for autonomous driving, and the Phoenix and UP-DRONE datasets for drone and quadruped navigation.
CONTROLS: Ablation experiments will compare our model against a traditional CNN-based RGB encoder and an event-driven encoder with uniform attention.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The incorporation of event-driven expert attention enables our model to achieve a 30% increase in segmentation accuracy over the best baseline in highly dynamic scenes, with a corresponding 20% decrease in computing resources. However, it may fail to effectively adapt to scenes with an overwhelming amount of extraneous events, potentially leading to decreased performance.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Safe and Reliable High-Frame-Rate Semantic Segmentation in Autonomous Systems
PROPOSAL: Building upon our previous proposals, we develop a framework for safe and reliable high-frame-rate semantic segmentation in autonomous systems. Our approach integrates the event-driven fusion model with incremental learning and incorporates a novel temporal reliability estimation module. This module assesses the temporal consistency of predicted segmentations and raises an alarm when the reliability threshold is exceeded. To train the model, we use a weighted combination of traditional segmentation accuracy and temporal reliability metrics. We demonstrate our approach on autonomous driving scenarios, comparing its performance with state-of-the-art event-driven methods and showing its ability to recover from inaccuracies and occlusions.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against traditional event-driven methods, as well as an ablation study to evaluate the contribution of the temporal reliability estimation module and incremental learning.
COST: 3900 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our approach exhibits robust performance, accurate segmentation, and reliable temporal consistency, setting a new standard for high-frame-rate semantic segmentation in autonomous systems. However, its safety features may be overly conservative in static environments, potentially leading to reduced performance in such scenarios.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Event-Driven Fusion in Augmented Reality: Applications in Drone Navigation
PROPOSAL: We explore the application of event-driven fusion in augmented reality (AR) for drone navigation. Our approach integrates the event-driven fusion model with a novel AR-based system that utilizes depth sensors and GPS data to provide accurate positioning and tracking information. By combining the RGB-event fusion model with AR-based system, we demonstrate the feasibility of real-time semantic segmentation for drone navigation in complex environments. We conduct experiments on the Phoenix and UP-DRONE datasets, showcasing the effectiveness of our approach in autonomous drone navigation.
CONTROLS: Experiments compare our approach against traditional event-driven methods and traditional AR-based systems, with ablation studies to evaluate the contribution of the RGB-event fusion model and AR-based system.
COST: 3600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our approach enables accurate and reliable semantic segmentation for drone navigation in complex environments, demonstrating its potential for real-world applications. However, its sensitivity to GPS signal loss or occlusion may impact performance in challenging environments.

PROPOSAL: To evaluate the practical impact of high-frame-rate semantic segmentation, we conduct a cost-benefit analysis of our approach in autonomous systems. PROPOSAL: Building upon our previous proposals, we develop a framework for safe and reliable high-frame-rate semantic segmentation in autonomous systems. Our approach integrates the event-driven fusion model with incremental learning and incorporates a novel temporal reliability estimation module. This module assesses the temporal consistency of predicted segmentations and raises an alarm when the reliability threshold is exceeded. To train the model, we use a weighted combination of traditional segmentation accuracy and temporal reliability metrics. We demonstrate our approach on autonomous driving scenarios, comparing its performance with state-of-the-art event-driven methods and showing its ability to recover from inaccuracies and occlusions.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach against traditional event-driven methods, as well as an ablation study to evaluate the contribution of the temporal reliability estimation module and incremental learning.
COST: 11700 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our approach exhibits robust performance, accurate segmentation, and reliable temporal consistency, setting a new standard for high-frame-rate semantic segmentation in autonomous systems. However, its safety features may be overly conservative in static environments, potentially leading to reduced performance in such scenarios.

By combining the RGB-event fusion model with AR-based system, we demonstrate the feasibility of real-time semantic segmentation for drone navigation in complex environments. We conduct experiments on the Phoenix and UP-DRONE datasets, showcasing the effectiveness of our approach in autonomous drone navigation.

TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Identity-Aware Contrastive Loss on 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: The goal of this experiment is to investigate the effect of adapting an identity-aware contrastive loss (IA-C Loss) from the 2D image synthesis literature to the task of 3D generation. Specifically, we will implement the IA-C Loss in a 3D generative model (e.g., [1] a variant of Diffusion++ [ Rooney et al., 2022 ]) and compare its performance to a baseline model using a standard reconstruction loss.
CONTROLS: Baseline controls include models with and without the IA-C Loss, and an ablation study to understand the effect of different hyperparameters (e.g., temperature, batch size).
COST: 8000
PREDICTION: We expect the IA-C Loss to significantly improve the identity preservation of 3D generations, especially for subjects with discriminative features (e.g., animals), but may struggle with subjects with less distinctive features (e.g., tables). However, the IA-C Loss might require more careful hyperparameter tuning to achieve optimal results.

[1] :Simple variants are better than advanced models for 3d and 4d photorealistic image generation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Personalized View-Consistent 3D Generation via View-Disentangled Representation Learning
PROPOSAL: This experiment aims to propose a novel 3D generation framework, D-Gen, that disentangles the view-invariant representation of a 3D object from its view-dependent appearance. D-Gen consists of two main components: a view-disentangled encoder and a view-aware decoder. The encoder learns a view-invariant representation of the object, while the decoder generates 3D assets that are consistent across different viewpoints. The framework will be trained on a synthetic dataset of 3D objects with varying viewpoints.
CONTROLS: Baseline controls include a standard 3D generation model (e.g., [3] Diffusion++ [ Rooney et al., 2022 ]) and an ablation study will be conducted to evaluate the importance of view-disentangled representation learning.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: We expect D-Gen to improve the view-consistency of generated 3D assets, especially for complex objects with multiple parts. However, the framework might require careful tuning of hyperparameters and could be computationally expensive for large-scale datasets.

[3] :Simple variants are better than advanced models for 3d and 4d photorealistic image generation

PROPOSAL: This experiment investigates the robustness of subject-driven generation to variability in input data, such as changes in pose, lighting, and occlusion. However, the study may also reveal that certain model variations or input preprocessing techniques can improve the model's robustness to variability.

TITLE: Utilizing Videogame Data for Personalized 3D Avatar Generation
PROPOSAL: Leverage vast, existing videogame datasets to train subject-driven 3D generative models. By leveraging character models, animations, and associated metadata from diverse games, we can develop a robust, data-efficient framework for generating personalized 3D avatars that captivate specific subjects' features and characteristics. PREDICTION: This dataset-based method has the potential to deliver compelling results in personalized 3D generation due to the use of high-quality, structured, and diverse videogame sources. However, transfer to entirely new domains or subject categories might be unpredictable, especially considering the content restrictions present in certain games.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Robust Personalized 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Develop an adversarial training framework that injects noise and contradictory prompts to improve the robustness of personalized 3D generative models. We will incorporate an adversary module that tries to mislead the model by generating contradictory outputs, which will be refined by the original generator. This process will ensure that the model is more resilient to changes in the input data and produces outputs that better preserve the identity of the target subject.
CONTROLS: Compare against state-of-the-art 3D generative models without adversarial training; evaluate the impact of different adversarial strategies on model performance
COST: 840 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This adversarial training approach may enhance the robustness of personalized 3D generation, but it might also lead to overfitting or mode collapse if not carefully tuned, considering the delicate balance between exploration and exploitation.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Subject-Agnostic Knowledge Distillation for Improved Transferability
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of subject-agnostic knowledge distillation to improve the transferability and generalizability of personalized 3D/4D generative models across different subjects and domains. We will train a teacher model on a diverse set of subjects and then distill the knowledge into a student model, leading to a more efficient and transferable model that requires fewer personalization steps.
CONTROLS: Compare against baseline models trained on single-subject datasets; evaluate the impact of teacher-student model architecture and knowledge distillation ratio on model transferability
COST: 1665.1 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach could enhance the transferability and generalizability of personalized 3D/4D generation, but its performance might suffer if the teacher model is biased towards a specific subject or domain, highlighting the need for careful selection of teacher and student models.

TITLE: Identity-Aware 4D Motion Synthesis using Temporal 3D Features
PROPOSAL: We will adapt a recent 4D (dynamic 3D) generation model (e.g., KalmanNet) to learn temporal 3D features that capture subject-specific motion patterns from a single video input. The model will attend to its learned subject embedding when predicting novel viewpoints, ensuring its output's motion consistency. Evaluation will focus on whether the model produces less deformed motion and improved subject identity maintenance when rendered from novel viewpoints. Controls include a baseline where the model still generates motions consistent with the input video but does so without using subject embeddings.

PREDICTION: Identity-Aware 4D Motion Synthesis will reduce deformed motion and improve subject identity maintenance, but it might suffer from viewpoint inconsistency in scenes with abrupt spatial transformations, such as running or falling animals.

This method integrates both personalized 3D modeling (proposed in point 1) and identity-aware 4D motion synthesis (proposed in point 2) with an additional consistency loss that encourages multiple 4D views generated from the same 3D reconstruction to remain consistent with each other. Controls include a baseline using either model independently.

COST: 1400
PREDICTION: The multi-view consistency-based synthesis method will show substantial improvements in identity preservation and overall realism. However, its performance might degrade in scenes with multiple subjects, as it primarily focuses on viewpoint consistency under a single subject ID.

TITLE: Content-Aware Adversarial Training for Personalized 3D and 4D Asset Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel, adversarial training framework that incorporates a content-aware discriminator to evaluate the generated 3D and 4D assets for identity preservation and spatial coherence. The discriminator will be trained on pairs of generated assets and curated datasets with high-quality, view-consistent, and subject-specific renderings. This allows us to directly compare generated output to real-world assets while maintaining a balance between identity preservation and environmental consistency. Controls include a standard adversarial training baseline without content-aware guidance.

COST: 2400
PREDICTION: The content-aware adversarial training framework will improve the quality and realism of generated 3D and 4D assets, particularly for scenes with diverse subject appearances and configurations. However, its computational overhead and sensitivity to discriminator hyperparameters may lead to decreased training efficiency.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: REVISED: Personalized 3D Reconstruction with Latent Space Disentanglement and Latency-Aware Constraints
PROPOSAL: We revise the initial proposal for personalized 3D reconstruction by incorporating latency-aware constraints from both 3D reconstruction and real-time rendering considerations. This revised method will impose temporal coherence requirements when generating novel viewpoints, staying in line with the subject's motion synchronization. This allows for subsequent 4D motions to be generated more coherently. Controls include the original ablation without latency-aware constraints.

COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The revised method will enhance the spatiotemporal coherence of generated 3D assets and support data-efficient 4D motion synthesis. However, it may require significant computational resources to accommodate latency-aware constraints and handle complex motions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Guarantee of Identity Preservation under Differential Privacy Constraints
PROPOSAL: We provide a theoretical analysis of identity preservation in personalized 3D and 4D models under differential privacy constraints, introducing a framework for quantifying and bounding the expressiveness-privacy tradeoff. This work establishes a theoretical foundation for designing identity-preserving generative models that provide strong privacy guarantees for sensitive data, including 3D scans and 4D video recordings of individuals.

COST: 4200
PREDICTION: The theoretical analysis will yield provably identity-preserving generative models, providing fundamental insights into the limits of data protection and the feasibility of personalized 3D and 4D models under various privacy settings. However, its experimental validation may require significant effort due to the tradeoff between expressiveness and privacy.

TITLE: Personalized 3D Reconstruction with Latent Space Disentanglement
PROPOSAL: We will train a state-of-the-art autoencoder-based 3D reconstruction model (e.g., Vladimir et al.'s autoencoder-based mesh reconstruction model) on a synthetic dataset of 3D meshes (e.g., ShapeNet) with personalized identities (learned embeddings) that distinguish different subjects. We will evaluate the ability of the model to reconstruct the subject's identity under different viewpoints and compare it to an ablation without personalized identities. Controls include a baseline using non-personalized 3D reconstruction models (e.g., VAE-based methods).

COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The proposed method will significantly outperform the ablation and the baseline in terms of reconstruction accuracy, but its performance might degrade when encountering subjects with complex or varied appearances.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Identity-Aware 4D Motion Synthesis using Temporal 3D Features
PROPOSAL: We will adapt a recent 4D (dynamic 3D) generation model (e.g., KalmanNet) to learn temporal 3D features that capture subject-specific motion patterns from a single video input. The model will attend to its learned subject embedding when predicting novel viewpoints, ensuring its output's motion consistency. Evaluation will focus on whether the model produces less deformed motion and improved subject identity maintenance when rendered from novel viewpoints. Controls include a baseline where the model still generates motions consistent with the input video but does so without using subject embeddings.

COST: 1800
PREDICTION: Identity-Aware 4D Motion Synthesis will reduce deformed motion and improve subject identity maintenance, but it might suffer from viewpoint inconsistency in scenes with abrupt spatial transformations, such as running or falling animals.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED: Identity-Aware 4D Motion Synthesis using Temporal 3D Features
PROPOSAL: We revise the previous proposal by additionally fine-tuning the 4D model on videos with subject-specific annotations (e.g., bounding box and text descriptions for the animal's name) using a weakly-supervised method, such as Masked-XPert. This will facilitate the model to learn invariant features under subject identity, allowing it to better preserve the subject's identity across viewpoints. Controls include the original baseline without subject fine-tuning.

COST: 3000
PREDICTION: The revised identity-aware 4D model will significantly improve subject identity preservation, but it might suffer from decreased realism due to the weakly-supervised fine-tuning on subject-specific annotations.

ACTION: REVISE 2

PROPOSAL: We revise the identity-aware 4D motion synthesis model by assessing and addressing viewpoint inconsistency in scenes with abrupt spatial transformations (e.g., running or falling animals). We will introduce a novel supplementary loss to reduce interpolation-based interpolation artifacts and possible viewpoint misalignments in scenes with multiple subjects, increasing the model's ability to maintain subject identity across novel viewpoints. Controls include the revised model without supplementary viewpoint loss.

COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The viewpoint inconsistency mitigation will improve the realism and coherence of generated scenes, but might lead to performance drops on scenes with complex motions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Reference-based Optimization for Personalized 3D/4D Generation
PROPOSAL: We will leverage self-attention and reference networks to dynamically generate a reference image or video that includes side and back views from the input single image or video, thus providing the model with additional view-specific cues for identity preservation during 3D/4D generation.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Vanilla model; Ablation studies on adaptive reference generation, including different self-attention variants, and orthogonal distance-based methods; Ablation study on reference-based vs. standalone optimization
COST: 640
PREDICTION: We expect considerable improvement in preserving identity, particularly for poly-articulated objects with a few examples of non-frontal views in the input, and attribute-less objects with non-variable observations; accessibility of custom-made references under constraints, such as model parameters and complexity of input data, will determine optimization costs.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multiview Regularization for Identity Preservation in 3D/4D Generation
PROPOSAL: We will regularize the 3D/4D generation process with a multiview constraint that encourages consistency across the generated views and consistency with the input views, using a consistency loss measuring the similarity between views and potentially incorporating thermal and transfer learning for better generalizability.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: No regularization; Baseline 2: Intersection of consistency loss with U-Net-based diffusion; Ablation studies on weights for thermal vs. transfer learning
COST: 1476
PREDICTION: Multiview regularization will presumably provide improved identity preservation, especially in distinguishing inter-object viewpoint variance from novel (imagined) objects viewpoints, but separately represents model equivariance with regard to generating functional 3D/4D images.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Reference-based Optimization for Personalized 3D/4D Generation
PROPOSAL: We will leverage self-attention and reference networks to dynamically generate a reference image or video that includes side and back views from the input single image or video, thus providing the model with additional view-specific cues for identity preservation during 3D/4D generation.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Vanilla model; Ablation studies on adaptive reference generation, including different self-attention variants, and orthogonal distance-based methods; Ablation study on reference-based vs. standalone optimization

ACTION: ADD

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Subject-Driven 3D Generation via Coarse-to-Fine Identity Mapping
PROPOSAL: Design an identity-aware 3D generative model that progressively refines the subject's appearance across novel viewpoints via a two-stage process: a coarse-stage uses a pre-trained subject-agnostic 3D model to generate a low-resolution, viewpoint-agnostic shape representation, and a fine-stage uses a learned identity mapping to refine the shape's appearance under various viewpoints. The identity mapping is learned from a small set of example images of the subject, which are aligned with their corresponding viewpoints using a differentiable registration module. We will use a Chamfer similarity loss to reward the generation of viewpoint-consistent and identity-preserving 3D shapes.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard 3D generation model without identity mapping, Ablation: 3D model without the coarse-stage shape representation
COST: 80 Giga-Float Operations (GFP)
PREDICTION: Our proposed model should outperform the baseline and ablation experiments in terms of semblance and viewpoint consistency, but may suffer from minor degeneracies in extreme viewpoint configurations due to insufficiencies in the shape registration module.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Minimizing Appearance Discrepancies in 4D Generation via View Synthesis Constraints
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel 4D generation model that explicitly minimizes appearance discrepancies across novel viewpoints by incorporating view synthesis constraints into the generative process. This is achieved by fine-tuning a pre-trained 4D generator on a dataset of images rendered from novel viewpoints of the same 3D scenes, using a contrastive loss that encourages the generation of viewpoint-consistent appearance. We will use the CARLA dataset as a synthetic benchmark for testing our proposed approach.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard 4D generation model without view synthesis constraints; Ablation: 4D model with view synthesis constraints but without fine-tuning
COST: 510 Giga-Float Operations (GFP)
PREDICTION: Our proposed model should significantly outperform the baseline and ablation experiments in terms of viewpoint consistency and appearance preservation, but may struggle with minor overfitting on the CARLA dataset due to the dataset's relatively small size and distribution.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Personalized Text-to-3D and Text-to-4D Generation via Subject-Aware Text Embeddings
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel method for personalized text-to-3D and text-to-4D generation that incorporates subject-aware text embeddings to capture the semantic identity of the subject. We will additionally use a graph-based attention mechanism to selectively attend to parts of the text that are most relevant to the subject's appearance. This is achieved by combining a pre-trained language model with a 3D or 4D generator that has been fine-tuned on a dataset of text-to-image or text-to-video pairs.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard text-to-3D or text-to-4D model without subject-aware text embeddings; Ablation: text-to-3D or text-to-4D model with subject-aware text embeddings but without graph-based attention
COST: 1170 Giga-Float Operations (GFP)
PREDICTION: Our proposed model should outperform the baseline and ablation experiments in terms of subject accuracy and visual coherence, but may suffer from minor text-to-image or text-to-video hallucination effects due to the limitations of the pre-trained language model.

TITLE: Adversarial Identity Perturbations for Improved Viewpoint Consistency
PROPOSAL: Develop an adversarial training framework that injects perturbations into the identity embedding of the subject to improve viewpoint consistency in 3D and 4D generation. Specifically, we will train a discriminator to distinguish between the original and perturbed identity embeddings, and use this adversarial loss to regularize the generator and improve its ability to preserve the subject's identity across viewpoints.

COST: 1378 Giga-Float Operations (GFP)

TITLE: Latent Space Disentanglement for Viewpoint-Agnostic Subject Identity
PROPOSAL: Investigate the benefits of latent space disentanglement for viewpoint-agnostic subject identity in 3D and 4D generation. We will employ a disentanglement-based approach to decouple the subject's identity and viewpoint information in the latent space of a pre-trained generator. This is achieved by training an additional encoder that maps the input image to a disentangled latent space, and then generating the 3D or 4D asset from this disentangled latent representation.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Subject-Driven 3D Generation via Coarse-to-Fine Identity Mapping
PROPOSAL: Design an identity-aware 3D generative model that progressively refines the subject's appearance across novel viewpoints via a two-stage process: a coarse-stage uses a pre-trained subject-agnostic 3D model to generate a low-resolution, viewpoint-agnostic shape representation, and a fine-stage uses a learned identity mapping to refine the shape's appearance under various viewpoints. The identity mapping is learned from a small set of example images of the subject, which are aligned with their corresponding viewpoints using a differentiable registration module. We will use a Chamfer similarity loss to reward the generation of viewpoint-consistent and identity-preserving 3D shapes.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard 3D generation model without identity mapping, Ablation: 3D model without the coarse-stage shape representation
COST: 240 Giga-Float Operations (GFP)
PREDICTION: Our proposed model should outperform the baseline and ablation experiments in terms of semblance and viewpoint consistency, but may suffer from minor degeneracies in extreme viewpoint configurations due to insufficiencies in the shape registration module.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Minimizing Appearance Discrepancies in 4D Generation via View Synthesis Constraints
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel 4D generation model that explicitly minimizes appearance discrepancies across novel viewpoints by incorporating view synthesis constraints into the generative process. This is achieved by fine-tuning a pre-trained 4D generator on a dataset of images rendered from novel viewpoints of the same 3D scenes, using a contrastive loss that encourages the generation of viewpoint-consistent appearance. We will use the CARLA dataset as a synthetic benchmark for testing our proposed approach.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard 4D generation model without view synthesis constraints; Ablation: 4D model with view synthesis constraints but without fine-tuning
COST: 1528 Giga-Float Operations (GFP)
PREDICTION: Our proposed model should significantly outperform the baseline and ablation experiments in terms of viewpoint consistency and appearance preservation, but may struggle with minor overfitting on the CARLA dataset due to the dataset's relatively small size and distribution.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Personalized Text-to-3D and Text-to-4D Generation via Subject-Aware Text Embeddings
PROPOSAL: Propose a novel method for personalized text-to-3D and text-to-4D generation that incorporates subject-aware text embeddings to capture the semantic identity of the subject. We will additionally use a graph-based attention mechanism to selectively attend to parts of the text that are most relevant to the subject's appearance. This is achieved by combining a pre-trained language model with a 3D or 4D generator that has been fine-tuned on a dataset of text-to-image or text-to-video pairs.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard text-to-3D or text-to-4D model without subject-aware text embeddings; Ablation: text-to-3D or text-to-4D model with subject-aware text embeddings but without graph-based attention
COST: 3510 Giga-Float Operations (GFP)
PREDICTION: Our proposed model should outperform the baseline and ablation experiments in terms of subject accuracy and visual coherence, but may suffer from minor text-to-image or text-to-video hallucination effects due to the limitations of the pre-trained language model.

TITLE: Subject-Driven 3D Generation via Coarse-to-Fine Identity Mapping

This allows the model to learn a more accurate and subject-specific shape representation in the coarse stage.

TITLE: Adversarial Identity Perturbations for Improved Viewpoint Consistency
PROPOSAL: Develop an adversarial training framework that injects perturbations into the identity embedding of the subject to improve viewpoint consistency in 3D and 4D generation. Specifically, we will train a discriminator to distinguish between the original and perturbed identity embeddings, and use this adversarial loss to regularize the generator and improve its ability to preserve the subject's identity across viewpoints.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Latent Space Disentanglement for Viewpoint-Agnostic Subject Identity
PROPOSAL: Investigate the benefits of latent space disentanglement for viewpoint-agnostic subject identity in 3D and 4D generation. We will employ a disentanglement-based approach to decouple the subject's identity and viewpoint information in the latent space of a pre-trained generator. This is achieved by training an additional encoder that maps the input image to a disentangled latent space, and then generating the 3D or 4D asset from this disentangled latent representation.

However, the uncertainty estimates may introduce additional computational overhead and require careful optimization to avoid overfitting to the specific uncertainty modeling.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Draft Model Compatibility on Cascade Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: Perform an ablation study on the effect of draft model compatibility on the performance and speedup of cascade speculative decoding. TITLE: Dynamically Adapting Cascade Schedules Using Cost-Optimization
PROPOSAL: Propose a dynamic scheduling framework that adaptively selects which draft model to use and how many tokens to draft at each cascade level during inference. This framework will be trained using reinforcement learning to minimize the total walltime for the cascade, while meeting a given acceptance rate threshold, and then evaluated on real-world benchmarks. Evaluate the framework's ability to optimize for different acceptance rates, token lengths, and model termination conditions (e.g., F1-score above 0.9, BLEU-4 above 5). Estimate the efficiency of the proposed approach using real-world datasets (WiKiText, Multi30k, SummarySent, SQuAD).
CONTROLS: Two baselines: 1) a pre-defined fixed cascade schedule, and 2) a greedy approach that always chooses the next model with the highest acceptance rate.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The results will demonstrate that adaptive scheduling achieves significant speedup benefits, outperforming the fixed scheduling and greedy approaches especially in situations where the acceptance rate is vary across different runtime or where there is more depth to take from typical data context.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Cascade Effectiveness with Retrieval-Augmented Drafting
PROPOSAL: Compare the speedup offered by a cascade of trained and untrained self-speculative methods to that of a standard retrieval-based drafter on a standard speculative decoding benchmark (e.g., the break-even point between retrieval-based drafting and standard decoding). Evaluate various standard benchmarks in real-world applications (LLM inference acceleration, multi-turn conversation, machine translation, and summarization) on real-world datasets (e.g., WikiText, Multi30k, CNN/Daily Mail), using the Walltime metric, average response time, and+n-gram overlap with the ground truth.
CONTROLS: Standard speculative decoding with a single model, retrieval-based drafting (e.g., prompt lookup decoding) and various standard self-speculative methods (e.g., EAGLE, Lookahead decoding), along with a re-implementation of BiTA, LayerSkip, and the Jacobi-style parallel decoding.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The results will show substantial speedup benefits from the use of trained cascade models, comparable to those from using separate trained models, while the untrained cascade methods should show slower improvements but should approach them as the cascade length increases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dynamically Adapting Cascade Schedules Using Cost-Optimization
PROPOSAL: Propose a dynamic scheduling framework that adaptively selects which draft model to use and how many tokens to draft at each cascade level during inference. This framework will be trained using reinforcement learning to minimize the total walltime for the cascade, while meeting a given acceptance rate threshold, and then evaluated on real-world benchmarks. Evaluate the framework's ability to optimize for different acceptance rates, token lengths, and model termination conditions (e.g., F1-score above 0.9, BLEU-4 above 5). Estimate the efficiency of the proposed approach using real-world datasets (WiKiText, Multi30k, SummarySent, SQuAD).
CONTROLS: Two baselines: 1) a pre-defined fixed cascade schedule, and 2) a greedy approach that always chooses the next model with the highest acceptance rate.
COST: 2700
PREDICTION: The results will demonstrate that adaptive scheduling achieves significant speedup benefits, outperforming the fixed scheduling and greedy approaches especially in situations where the acceptance rate is vary across different runtime or where there is more depth to take from typical data context.

In addition to the previous evaluation metrics, we will measure the number of tokens processed per second for the cascade approaches and standard speculative decoding. This will provide insight into the effect of cascade scheduling on overall system performance and efficiency.
CONTROLS: Unchanged.
COST: 1800 (since the changes will likely require some re-evaluation but not a completely new run-through)
PREDICTION: This change will further emphasize the benefits of cascade speculative decoding in terms of system efficiency and throughput, highlighting its practical applications in real-world scenarios where processing large volumes of text is critical.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Experimental Evaluation of DelegateQA for Self-Speculative Cascades
PROPOSAL: We propose a new experimental methodology to investigate the effectiveness of combining existing training-free self-speculative decoding methods with retrieval-based drafting methods in a cascade architecture, using DelegateQA as the base model. We will first implement DelegateQA, a state-of-the-art few-shot learning model that can be used for self-speculative decoding, and integrate it with a cache-based retriever to provide retrieval-based draft tokens. We will then test various self-speculative acceleration techniques on top of the DelegateQA cascades, examining the trade-offs between latency, quality, and the number of cascade rounds.
CONTROLS: We will compare these cascade architectures to standard speculative decoding with a single larger model, as well as to cascades using separately trained draft models from EAGLE and Medusa.
COST: 840 gpu-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to observe significant speedup over standard speculative decoding, with DelegateQA cascades providing a sweet spot between speed and quality. However, the actual performance may depend on scheduling choices and the families of self-speculative methods used.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Cascade Configuration using Gradient-Free Optimization
PROPOSAL: We propose an adaptive cascade configuration method that uses gradient-free optimization techniques to search for the optimal draft model selection and switching points, as well as the number of tokens to draft at each level, in real-time during inference. We will use black-box optimization methods such as Bayesian optimization and genetic algorithms to learn the best cascade schedule for the DelegateQA cascades on-the-fly. To control the additional inference latency introduced by the adaptive optimization, we will use a modest-sized neural network to estimate the expected walltime improvement as a function of the three variables mentioned, and sample from the learned distribution during inference.
CONTROLS: We will compare the adaptive cascade configuration to the fixed cascade configuration from the baseline experiment, as well as to the retrieval-based drafter alone.
COST: 1345.678925 gpu-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to observe a significant reduction in walltime relative to the fixed cascade configuration, with the best performance achievable under optimal conditions, which may not always be possible in practice due to the discrete nature of the sampling process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Cascade Schedules under Uncertainty
PROPOSAL: We propose a theoretical framework to analyze the optimal cascade schedules under uncertainty about the acceptance rates and computational costs of self-speculative acceleration techniques. We will model the uncertainty using probability distributions over the acceptance rates and costs, and derive a stochastic programming formulation to determine the optimal cascade schedule. We will then investigate the impact of the uncertainty on the optimal cascade schedule and the resulting walltime improvement.
CONTROLS: We will consider various probability distributions and uncertainty models, and compare the results to the case with complete knowledge of the acceptance rates and costs.
COST: 2000 gpu-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our theoretical framework to provide new insights into the design of optimal cascade schedules under uncertainty, and our numerical experiments to show that accounting for uncertainty can lead to significantly improved performance in real-world applications. However, the computational cost of solving the stochastic programming formulation may be high, limiting its practical applicability.

TITLE: On-the-Fly Efficacy Analysis of Cascade Schedules under Dynamic Task Conditions
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel, on-the-fly efficacy analysis framework to monitor and adapt the cascade schedule in response to dynamic changes in the task conditions. We will use online statistical methods to track the performance of the cascade schedule and detect deviations from the expected behavior. Based on this analysis, we will dynamically adjust the cascade schedule to ensure optimal performance, potentially involving changes to the selection of self-speculative methods, the number of lookahead iterations, and the order of cascade levels.
CONTROLS: We will compare the results to static cascade schedules and examine the benefits of the on-the-fly efficacy analysis in terms of adaptability and overall performance.
COST: 3322 gpu-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the on-the-fly efficacy analysis framework to enable adaptability to dynamic task conditions and improve the overall performance of the cascade schedule. However, the online statistical methods may introduce additional computational overhead and the adaptability of the cascade schedule may not always align with the optimal solution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Cascade Scheduling with Inference-Time Hyperparameter Tuning
PROPOSAL: We introduce an adaptive scheduling technique that dynamically chooses the draft model to use and the number of tokens to draft at each level of the cascade during inference. This is achieved by analyzing the target model's hidden states and using this information to adjust the hyperparameters for the current cascade level. We compare the walltime improvement and quality of output for our adaptive scheduling method and the fixed schedule with various baselines on Llama and Qwen LLMs for the same datasets as in experiment 1.
CONTROLS: Fixed schedule with and without the retrieval-based drafter, Lookahead Decoding without the cascade, using the same grid search over Lookahead parameters, cascade configurations with two-stage fixed cascade schedules (different random hyperparameters).
COST: 81000
PREDICTION: We expect that our adaptive scheduling method will provide the largest speedup over the fixed schedule, close to the performance of an ideal adaptive oracle that knows the sequence’s acceptance rate in advance, which will be used for comparisons in a later experiment. Unfortunately, performance may drop due to the added computational overhead of inference-time hyperparameter tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating BERT-based Relative Absolute Reward Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to LLM reward modeling by combining the strengths of discriminative and generative models. Our method, denoted as BERT-RARE, appends a BERT-based module to the value head of a base model, enabling it to learn both relative and absolute preferences. This allows the model to provide calibrated scores with a probabilistic interpretation. TITLE: Adversarial Calibration of Generative Reward Models
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel training paradigm for generative reward models, centered around adversarial calibration. By adding a discriminator that enforces calibrated and probabilistic outputs from the generative model, we aim to reduce the need for costly pointwise supervision in calibration. Furthermore, our approach ensures that the model learns absolute quality judgments, capturing the inherent uncertainty in preference data. We adapt our method to the ArmoRM generative reward model and evaluate its performance on real-world benchmarks for math reasoning, code generation, and role-play dialogue.

PREDICTION: Our results are expected to show improved calibration and reduced uncertainty in the generative model's outputs, leading to enhanced performance in accounting for annotator disagreement and ambiguity in preference data. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Active Learning for Scalable Reward Function Adaptation
PROPOSAL: To bridge the gap between absolute quality judgments and limited annotations, we propose an active learning framework for reward function adaptation. Our approach, denoted as ALRA, selects the most informative samples from a large pool of unlabeled data, allowing for efficient adaptation of the reward function to a new domain using only a few high-quality annotations. We demonstrate ALRA's ability to adapt LLM reward functions to various domains, including code generation and chatbot safety, while maintaining state-of-the-art performance on ranking accuracy.
CONTROLS: We compare ALRA to a baseline using randomly selected samples and to a domain-adaptation method that relies on extensive human labeling. We also evaluate ALRA's performance on several real-world benchmarks for LLM reward modeling.
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: We expect ALRA to achieve significant reductions in the number of annotations required for domain adaptation, leading to substantial cost savings. However, we anticipate that its performance might degrade slightly in extremely domain-adversarial scenarios.

TITLE: A Theoretical Analysis of Reward Model Calibration using Concentration Inequalities
PROPOSAL: We provide a theoretical analysis of the calibration properties of reward models, focusing on tools from probability theory, specifically concentration inequalities. We establish bounds on the probability of the reward model's outputs deviating from the true preferences of the annotator, providing insights into the role of the reward model's complexity and the size of the dataset in achieving well-calibrated scores. Our analysis applies to reward models proposed in this research.
CONTROLS: Our results will be compared to existing theoretical guarantees for reward model calibration, as well as empirical results from state-of-the-art reward models like BERT-RARE and MetaRF.
COST: 200 ( note: since this is a theoretical result, it does not require significant computational resources )
PREDICTION: Our theoretical results are expected to provide fundamental insights into the calibration properties of reward models and establish a new framework for understanding the role of model complexity and dataset size in achieving well-calibrated scores.

PROPOSAL: We propose a framework for selecting the optimal reward model from a set of candidate models based on a multi-objective formulation of the welfare criterion, which maximizes the expected utility achieved by the LLM. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Triple-Task Learning for Hybrid Reward Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a triple-task learning framework that combines three objectives: (1) ranking (to learn relative preferences), (2) calibration (to learn absolute quality scores), and (3) regression (to learn confidence scores). The framework leverages a shared base model and two task-specific heads, each optimized using a different task-specific loss function. The ranking head is optimized using the Bradley-Terry objective, the calibration head is optimized using a log-likelihood loss, and the regression head is optimized using a mean squared error loss. By learning these three tasks simultaneously, the model can leverage the strengths of both discriminative and generative reward models, while also addressing their respective weaknesses. This approach enables the model to learn a more comprehensive and nuanced representation of human preferences.
CONTROLS: (A) naive baseline where scores helpfully replace traditional discriminative ahead even without pair ratings, and (B) standard reinforcement reward assistant training iteration without multi-task learning, and (C) discriminative reward model only trained for ranking task.
COST: (1152)
PREDICTION: Model achieves state-of-the-art performance in ranking, calibration, and confidence tasks, but may require more aggressive regularization to prevent overfitting due to the increased number of parameters.

TITLE: Triple-Task Learning for Hybrid Reward Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a triple-task learning framework that combines three objectives: (1) ranking (to learn relative preferences), (2) calibration (to learn absolute quality scores), and (3) regression (to learn confidence scores). The framework leverages a shared base model and two task-specific heads, each optimized using a different task-specific loss function. The ranking head is optimized using the Bradley-Terry objective, the calibration head is optimized using a log-likelihood loss, and the regression head is optimized using a mean squared error loss. By learning these three tasks simultaneously, the model can leverage the strengths of both discriminative and generative reward models, while also addressing their respective weaknesses. This approach enables the model to learn a more comprehensive and nuanced representation of human preferences.

TITLE: Flexible Reward Model with Uncertainty Estimation
PROPOSAL: We propose to investigate a hybrid reward model that combines the efficiency of discriminative models with the interpretability of generative ones. Our model, named HybridReward, uses a probabilistic output layer to estimate the uncertainty of the human preference signal, and a feedback mechanism to adaptively adjust the score threshold based on the uncertainty estimates. We will implement this model using a combination of Transformer architectures and a probabilistic output layer, such as the Alpha-Dense layer.
CONTROLS: We will compare HybridReward to state-of-the-art discriminative models (e.g., Skywork-Reward, InternLM2-Reward) and generative models (e.g., HelpSteer2-Preference, ArmoRM). We will also evaluate the effect of different types of uncertainty estimates (e.g., entropy, variance) on the model's performance.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: HybridReward should outperform both discriminative and generative models in terms of ranking accuracy, while providing more interpretable and calibrated scores. However, it may struggle with high-dimensional input spaces, and the cost of training the probabilistic output layer may be high.

TITLE: Reward Suffix Network for Absolute Quality Estimation via Conceptual Prompting and Training with Truncated Chain-of-Thought Critiques
PROPOSAL: Design a reward suffix network that leverages the output of a base LLM and a chain-of-thought generator to compute absolute quality scores for LLM responses. This is achieved through variant prompting and shorter chain-of-thought critiques than standard models. The suffix network computes alignment scores relative to a target response quality, in addition to computing quality scores based on the absolute quality of the input.
CONTROLS: Compare against current leading generative reward models and variants using quality-annotated datasets, specifically comparing against Celeb-10K evaluation dataset.
COST: 151200
PREDICTION: This proposal may achieve competitive performance in absolute quality estimation while leveraging the strengths of generative reward models and improve workflows through conceptual prompting. However, training this model may struggle due to an excessive computation load and slower inference times.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Contrastive Loss for Unbiased Utilization Signal Estimation
PROPOSAL: We design a new contrastive loss function to estimate the utilization of external context and internal knowledge in response generation. The loss is minimized by training a discriminator to distinguish between responses generated with and without access to the relevant external context. In the "with context" branch, the generator receives the query, the context, and generates a response. In the "without context" branch, the generator receives only the query and generates a response relying only on its internal knowledge. The discriminator predicts the probability that each response was generated with context access. During training, the generator's goal is to produce responses that are predictable by the discriminator, when context access is available, and unpredictable otherwise. This setup encourages the generator to utilize external context in a meaningful way and to avoid over-reliance on internal knowledge.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Training the generator with an epoch-based rehearsal curriculum, Baseline 2: Training the generator with a random masking of its input, Baseline 3: Training a simple heuristic-based discriminator that outputs 0.5 for all responses.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: The proposed approach should lead to a more accurate estimation of external context utilization, while the heuristic-based discriminator might oversimplify the task, leading to a less effective model overall.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Module Attention-Masked Language Model
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel multi-module attention-masked language model (MAML) architecture, where the model is divided into two parallel sub-networks: one that processes the external context and another that processes the query. The outputs of these sub-networks are then distilled into a single response. To discourage over-reliance on internal knowledge, we introduce attention masking: during training, the model randomly masks certain attention queries pointing towards the internal knowledge, and instead receives information from a learned embedding of the context. The embedding is conditioned on the context and the query, allowing the model to ground its response in the external context.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: A vanilla transformer-based retrieval-augmented generator, Baseline 2: A transformer-based generator with hand-selected attention heads and layers, Baseline 3: A competitive state-of-the-art retrieval-augmented generator.
COST: 540
PREDICTION: The proposed MAML architecture should significantly reduce hallucinations by promoting external context usage and discouraging internal knowledge over-reliance, but might require more computational resources to train.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Data Conditioning for Protocol Semantic Entropy Estimates
PROPOSAL: We propose that data conditioning, where external context is manipulated to induce regimes of high or low semantic entropy, can facilitate more accurate protocol semantic entropy estimates. We develop a novel data conditioning framework where we selectively amplify or attenuate relevant external context tokens, taking into consideration the input query, thus modulating semantic entropy. We then use probes to estimate the internal semantic entropy; when external context semantic entropy increases, and internal responds with reduced semantic entropy, we consider this a strong indication that the model has utilized the new contextual information, improving the reliability of information provided.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: Basic probes that don't leverage conditioning, Baseline 2: State-of-the-art probes that only use semantic entropy, without any data conditioning, Baseline 3: A simulator to test for the sensitivity of the probes to data quality.
COST: 690
PREDICTION: The proposed protocol should enable precise quantitative estimates of – internal knowledge dependency during – LLM work, even with manipulations ranging from – straightforward supervised methods to semi-supervised or unsupervised variants; the amount of conditioning might have a moderate-to-severe impact in its effects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Prior Knowledge Graph Embeddings for Context Grounding
PROPOSAL: We propose to incorporate prior knowledge graph embeddings into the retrieval-augmented generation model to better capture the contextual relationships and grounding aspects of the external context. Specifically, we augment the input context with learned graph embeddings that represent the keyword relationships and their associated semantic constraints. This allows the model to reason explicitly about the context, incorporate relevant background knowledge, and adapt the generated response accordingly. By leveraging the structure and semantics of the context, we enable more effective utilization of external context and more accurate detection of hallucinations.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: A vanilla retrieval-augmented generator, Baseline 2: A retrieval-augmented generator with a simple context embeddings, Baseline 3: A knowledge-augmented retrieval-augmented generator that uses weakly-supervised learning.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The proposed use of prior knowledge graph embeddings should lead to a more contextually-grounded retrieval-augmented generator, but their integration might require careful calibration to avoid over❆️reliance on the graph embeddings.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-Contextualized Auditing of Internal Knowledge Utilization
PROPOSAL: We introduce a novel auditing methodology to evaluate the utilization of internal knowledge on a per-contextual basis. By probing the model's responses with context-specific queries, we can assess the extent to which the model relies on internal knowledge versus external context for each specific context. This allows us to identify contexts where the model tends to over-rely on internal knowledge and hallucinate, and to develop targeted fine-tuning strategies to mitigate these issues. To facilitate this auditing process, we propose to allocate a dedicated perturbation space for per-contextualized audits, allowing the model to adapt to the specific contextual requirements.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: A simple context-aware probing mechanism, Baseline 2: A context-agnostic auditing approach, Baseline 3: A state-of-the-art auditing model specifically designed for generic knowledge testing.
COST: 1050
PREDICTION: The proposed per-contextualized auditing approach should offer a more nuanced understanding of internal knowledge utilization and hallucination, allowing for targeted interventions to improve model performance, however, it may add computational overhead during the auditing process.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint Training for Interleaved Interpretable Retrieval and Generation
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to jointly training the retrieval model and the generation model in an interleaved manner, where the retrieval model learns to retrieve relevant context given the query, and the generation model learns to generate responses based on the retrieved context. This approach allows for iterative refinement of both the retrieval and generation processes, promoting a more informed and contextually-grounded generation of responses. We implement an attention-sharing mechanism to encourage the generation model to focus on key aspects of the retrieved context and detect hallucinations based on the attention allocation of the generation model.
CONTROLS: Baseline 1: A vanilla retrieval-augmented generator, Baseline 2: A retrieval-augmented generator with pre-trained retrieval model, Baseline 3: A competitive state-of-the-art retrieval-augmented generator with joint training.
COST: 1345.678925
PREDICTION: The proposed joint training approach should lead to a more effective combination of retrieval and generation, reducing hallucinations and improving context grounding, but the added complexity may make model training and inference more computationally expensive.
