ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Occlusion-aware Latent 3D Representation for View-dependent Appearance
PROPOSAL: We'll implement a neural network architecture based on the NeRF model, that instead of predicting a density function solely from input rays, predicts a density function that accounts for view-dependent occlusion and appearance. This will be achieved by modifying the network to output an additional occlusion-aware term that can account for partial occlusions between objects. We'll train the network on a large dataset of real-world objects with associated multiview images.
CONTROLS: We'll compare our Occlusion-aware model to a NeRF model without the occlusion-aware term, as well as to a baseline occupancy grid representation that only accounts for geometry.
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: We expect the Occlusion-aware model to perform significantly better on tasks that require capturing view-dependent occlusion, such as latent 3D reconstruction and image-to-3D generation from views with partial occlusion. However, it may not outperform the baseline occupancy grid representation for tasks that focus solely on geometry.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Data-efficient Learning of Occlusion-aware Latents via Hierarchical Voxel Grids
PROPOSAL: To improve upon proposal 1 by better handling the spatial complexity of real-world objects, we'll introduce a hierarchical voxel grid structure that progressively refines the 3D representation. This will allow us to learn a more detailed occlusion-aware representation with minimal increase in trainable parameters and computational cost. The hierarchical architecture will consist of multiple scales of voxel grids, each encoding increasingly detailed geometry and appearance information.
CONTROLS: We'll compare our Hierarchical Voxel Grid model to the Occlusion-aware model from proposal 1, as well as to a state-of-the-art dense voxel grid representation.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: We expect the Hierarchical Voxel Grid model to significantly outperform the Occlusion-aware model by accurately capturing detailed geometry and occlusion patterns, while also surpassing the dense voxel grid baseline for its ability to represent view-dependent appearance effectively.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bridge Between Geometry and Appearance: Multimodal Fusion for 3D Latents
PROPOSAL: To further address the challenge of jointly representing geometry and appearance, we'll investigate multimodal fusion techniques that allow for simultaneous learning of both modalities within a single 3D latent space. This will be achieved by introducing a novel fusion module that merges information from geometry and appearance streams within the hierarchical voxel grid structure. We'll utilize a shared latent code to couple the geometry and appearance information, enabling the model to learn representations that are consistent across different views and illumination conditions.
CONTROLS: We'll compare our Multimodal Fusion model to both the Occlusion-aware model and the Hierarchical Voxel Grid model from previous proposals, as well as to a baseline model that simply concatenates geometry and appearance features.
COST: 24000
PREDICTION: We expect the Multimodal Fusion model to improve over the existing proposals by robustly capturing both geometric and appearance information, and to generalize well to new viewpoints and lighting conditions. However, it may require more sophisticated regularization techniques to avoid mode collapse and ensure stable training.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Refining Multimodal Fusion for 3D Latents
PROPOSAL: We'll refine the Multimodal Fusion model from proposal 3 by introducing a dynamic weighting scheme for the fusion module. This will allow the model to adaptively balance the contributions of geometry and appearance information based on the specific task requirements and the input data distribution. Specifically, we'll use a learned weighting mechanism that is conditioned on the input data, enabling the model to focus on the most relevant modality for each specific task.
CONTROLS: We'll compare the refined Multimodal Fusion model to the original version, as well as to a baseline model with a fixed weighting scheme for fusion.
COST: 20000 ( Revised from 24000 to focus on refining the existing work)
PREDICTION: We expect the refined Multimodal Fusion model to improve upon the original version by more effectively adapting to the task requirements and input data distribution, leading to better performance on a range of 3D tasks. However, it may require additional training data or regularization techniques to ensure stable training and avoid over-specialization.

ACTION: REVISE

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: View-Consistent 3D Reconstruction with Neural Reflection Fields
PROPOSAL: Perform an experiment to adapt the Neural Reflection Fields (NRF) architecture to jointly reconstruct the 3D mesh of an object and its appearance from a single RGB image. Implement a modified version of NRF that outputs a probabilistic occupancy map with NeRF's differential volumes formulation, allowing it to encode both geometry and appearance information. Evaluate the model's performance on the DTU and ICML2019 benchmarks, comparing it to state-of-the-art geometry-only and appearance-only methods.
CONTROLS: Compare to pix2vols, pi-turbo, and difface, using ablating different components of the NRF architecture to isolate their contributions to the results. Also, consider using StyleRig as a baseline for view-consistent 3D reconstruction.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed method should outperform current geometry-only approaches on DTU while showing comparable or improved results on ICML2019, thanks to its ability to capture view-dependent effects. However, it might struggle to handle extremely complex object appearances or novel views due to the ambiguity in the occupancy map.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning Coherent 3D-Appearance Embeddings with a View-Sensitive Spherical Grid
PROPOSAL: Design an experiment to develop a novel 3D-appearance embedding method that incorporates a view-sensitive spherical grid to encode and reason about spatially coherent appearance information. This approach aims to represent objects as 3D volumes with appearance radiance that varies with view direction, while still capturing the underlying geometry. Train a 3D Generator-Conditioned Neural Radiance Field (GCNeRF) model using ICLR's ShapeNetCore and Facades datasets to evaluate the model's ability to generate coherent and photo-realistic views from arbitrary angles.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed method to GCNeRF with a view-invariant spherical grid and a vanilla GCNeRF without view sensitivity, and investigate the impact of different grid orientations and resolutions on the results.
COST: 3000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed approach should demonstrate improved view-consistency and generate photorealistic views across various angles, outperforming the GCNeRF baseline. However, it might be challenging to maintain this performance when dealing with very fine-grained appearances or extreme occlusions.

TITLE: View-Aware Conditional Autoregressive Models for 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Develop an experiment using a view-aware conditional autoregressive (CAR) model for 3D reconstruction. This model would leverage the conditional dependencies between pixels in an image to jointly infer the object's geometry and appearance. Train the model on the IMLS dataset and FlickerSketch dataset to evaluate its ability to capture view-dependent effects and coherence. Investigate the effectiveness of different CAR models, including CAR with Gaussian conditional distributions and CAR with learned mean and variance functions.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed method to other 3D reconstruction approaches, such as DeepSDF and Mesh R-CNN, and ablate different components of the CAR model to understand its performance.
COST: 6000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The view-aware CAR model is expected to demonstrate improved coherence and view-consistency, especially on datasets with complex geometry and appearance. However, its computational cost and potentially slow inference might hinder its practical applicability.

TITLE: Multi-View Consistency Metric for 3D Reconstruction Evaluation
PROPOSAL: Develop a novel multi-view consistency metric that evaluates the accuracy and coherence of 3D reconstructions across multiple viewpoints. This metric will be based on the concept of view-similarity scores calculated using deep neural network features. Train and test the proposed metric on several benchmark datasets to demonstrate its effectiveness and fairness in assessing 3D reconstruction methods.

PROPOSAL: Develop a novel approach for 3D scene reconstruction from multiple viewpoints using physics-informed neural networks (PINNs). However, its formulation may require careful tuning of the physical parameters and might be prone to overfitting if not properly regularized.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: True Skeleton Loss for Image AR Models
PROPOSAL: We introduce the True Skeleton Loss (TSL) to regularize the generator during training. TSL encourages the generator to preserve the structural relationships between tokens in the teacher AR model, which is typically learned implicitly through the reconstruction loss. This is done by training a auxiliary model to predict the skeleton of the ground-truth token sequence (i.e., the connections between adjacent tokens) from the output of the generator. We use a graph convolutional network as the auxiliary model and optimize it to minimize the difference between its predictions and the ground-truth skeleton.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Regular reconstruction loss only
- Baseline 2: Regular reconstruction loss with a traditional regularization technique (e.g., dropout or weight decay)
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: TSL should help preserve structural relationships between tokens and improve the quality of the generated sequences. However, it might over-regularize the generator, leading to suboptimal performance on more complex tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Conditional Adversarial Generator for Image AR Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a conditional adversarial generator that leverages a discriminator to enforce the generator to produce tokens that are not only structurally consistent with the teacher AR model but also visually realistic. The discriminator is trained to distinguish between the output of the generator and a set of real token sequences sampled from the teacher AR model. We use a conditional variant of the StyleGAN discriminator, which takes the output of the generator and the current state of the token sequence as input.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Generator trained with TSL (from proposal 1) and reconstruction loss
- Baseline 2: Generator trained without any regularization
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The conditional adversarial generator should improve the quality of the generated sequences by forcing the generator to produce tokens that are both structurally consistent and visually realistic. However, it might be challenging to balance the generator's ability to generate realistic tokens with the need to maintain structural consistency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Token Representation Learning
PROPOSAL: We explore the use of hierarchical token representations to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the generator. Inspired by the success of hierarchical representations in computer vision, we propose to use a hierarchical architecture to represent each token as a structured representation consisting of a coarse-grained (low-dimensional) feature and a fine-grained (high-dimensional) feature. We use a multi-resolution convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the hierarchical representations, where the coarse-grained feature captures the global properties of the token and the fine-grained feature captures the local details.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Generator trained with unconditional adversarial loss
- Baseline 2: Generator trained with TSL (from proposal 1) and unconditional adversarial loss
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: The hierarchical token representation learning approach should allow the generator to capture more complex token structures and improve the quality of the generated sequences. However, it might be challenging to balance the trade-off between the coarse-grained and fine-grained features and the increased computational cost of the hierarchical architecture.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: True Skeleton Loss for Image AR Models
PROPOSAL: We introduce the True Skeleton Loss (TSL) to regularize the generator during training. TSL encourages the generator to preserve the structural relationships between tokens in the teacher AR model, which is typically learned implicitly through the reconstruction loss. This is done by training a auxiliary model to predict the skeleton of the ground-truth token sequence (i.e., the connections between adjacent tokens) from the output of the generator. We use a graph convolutional network as the auxiliary model and optimize it to minimize the difference between its predictions and the ground-truth skeleton.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Regular reconstruction loss only
- Baseline 2: Regular reconstruction loss with a traditional regularization technique (e.g., dropout or weight decay)
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: TSL should help preserve structural relationships between tokens and improve the quality of the generated sequences. However, it might over-regularize the generator, leading to suboptimal performance on more complex tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Conditional Adversarial Generator for Image AR Models
PROPOSAL: We propose a conditional adversarial generator that leverages a discriminator to enforce the generator to produce tokens that are not only structurally consistent with the teacher AR model but also visually realistic. The discriminator is trained to distinguish between the output of the generator and a set of real token sequences sampled from the teacher AR model. We use a conditional variant of the StyleGAN discriminator, which takes the output of the generator and the current state of the token sequence as input.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Generator trained with TSL (from proposal 1) and reconstruction loss
- Baseline 2: Generator trained without any regularization
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: The conditional adversarial generator should improve the quality of the generated sequences by forcing the generator to produce tokens that are both structurally consistent and visually realistic. However, it might be challenging to balance the generator's ability to generate realistic tokens with the need to maintain structural consistency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Token Representation Learning
PROPOSAL: We explore the use of hierarchical token representations to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the generator. Inspired by the success of hierarchical representations in computer vision, we propose to use a hierarchical architecture to represent each token as a structured representation consisting of a coarse-grained (low-dimensional) feature and a fine-grained (high-dimensional) feature. We use a multi-resolution convolutional neural network (CNN) to learn the hierarchical representations, where the coarse-grained feature captures the global properties of the token and the fine-grained feature captures the local details.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Generator trained with unconditional adversarial loss
- Baseline 2: Generator trained with TSL (from proposal 1) and unconditional adversarial loss
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: The hierarchical token representation learning approach should allow the generator to capture more complex token structures and improve the quality of the generated sequences. However, it might be challenging to balance the trade-off between the coarse-grained and fine-grained features and the increased computational cost of the hierarchical architecture.

Instead of using a separate multi-resolution CNN to learn the hierarchical representations, we use a shared neural network to learn a joint embedding of the input noise and the coarse-grained feature, and then decode the generated token sequence using the fine-grained feature. This allows the generator to learn more complex token structures and improve the quality of the generated sequences.

PROPOSAL: We investigate different noise exploration strategies to better utilize the input noise when training the generator. Specifically, we propose to use importance-sampled noise, which assigns different weights to different noise samples based on their likelihood under the teacher AR model. We also propose to use noise contrastive estimation, which learns a noise discriminator to predict whether a given noise sample is from the input distribution or a fixed noise distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Direct Prediction Method
PROPOSAL: Develop a Direct Prediction Method (DPM) that trains a new generator to directly predict the entire token sequence from a latent variable, without relying on a predefined noise-to-data mapping. The generator takes the latent variable as input and outputs a sequence of tokens, where each token is a discrete codebook index. The generator is trained using a loss function that measures the similarity between the predicted token sequence and the token sequence sampled from the teacher AR model.
CONTROLS: Train DPM using a teacher AR model with and without flow matching (for comparison), and compare DPM to existing one-step methods (DD1) on real-world datasets.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: DPM achieves competitive results with DD1 on real-world datasets, but may struggle with very large codebooks due to the difficulty of directly predicting a sequence of discrete indices.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modeling Codebook Correlations
PROPOSAL: Examine the role of codebook correlations in the performance of one-step generators, by introducing a new loss function that captures the similarity between codebook entries. This can help guide the generator to learn more meaningful correlations between tokens in the codebook. The new loss function, called Correlation Loss, is added to the existing loss function of the Direct Prediction Method, allowing us to jointly learn token sequences and codebook correlations.
CONTROLS: Experiment with the Correlation Loss in concert with DPM on several real-world datasets, including images of varying complexity and resolution.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Incorporating Correlation Loss with DPM significantly improves performance on complex images, where the additional modeling capacity of the codebook correlations is crucial for high-quality token sequences.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Token Generation
PROPOSAL: Explore the possibility of generating tokens in a hierarchical manner, where the generator predicts a coarse-grained token sequence first and then refines it with a secondary generator that produces more detailed tokens. This approach could be particularly effective when the teacher AR model produces token sequences with a clear hierarchical structure. We introduce a two-stage generator, (1) a Pyramid Generator that predicts coarse-grained tokens and (2) a Refiner that predicts finer-grained tokens, to capture both the overall structure and the local details of the input.
CONTROLS: Experiment with the Hierarchical Token Generation framework in conjunction with the Correlation Loss on real-world datasets, and compare its performance to existing one-step methods.
COST: 768
PREDICTION: The Hierarchical Token Generation framework achieves high-quality token sequences on a variety of real-world datasets, especially those with complex and structured patterns, by dividing the task into more manageable sub-problems.

This can help prevent the model from making drastic mistakes, especially when the Pyramid Generator predicts a coarse token sequence that is close to the correct solution but not exact.

The generator will learn a direct mapping from the latent space to the token sequence space, without relying on flow matching or a predefined noise-to-data mapping. We will use a standard Autoencoder-based architecture with a Transformer decoder, and the contrastive loss will be computed between the generator's output and the teacher AR model's output for a batch of random noise inputs.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Explicit Objectives for Routing Diversity in Mixture-of-Experts
PROPOSAL: We investigate a combinatorial version of the routing objective, where we add pairwise losses to the original load-balancing loss. Instead of merely promoting uniform expert usage, the new objective encourages diverse combinations of experts across the same token sets, with a target of selecting at least one expert from an optimal partition of tokens given the available experts. We compute the optimal partition via graph clustering.
CONTROLS: We compare to a baseline of standard load-balancing objectives, and ablate our method by considering ablated version of the pairwise losses, all while fine-tuning with the same set of hyperparameters.
COST: 20000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: With this objective, experts are more likely to be trained on non-overlapping data distributions, reducing the incidence of expert homogenization. This in turn should improve language modeling performance and enable more efficient generalization in downstream tasks. I predict a 5% absolute improvement in perplexity on the benchmark evaluation, particularly in tasks with high functional specialization, but also a risky failure mode where the more rigid routing constraints might inadvertently freeze some of the experts and lead to over-specialization for some tasks.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Expert Specialization
PROPOSAL: In addition to the combinatorial routing objective, we introduce a hierarchical structure for the experts. We divide the input space into a hierarchical set of sub-spaces, where each expert in a deeper layer is fine-grained and can specialize in a specific, but smaller subset of the input space. This is defined through a top-down scheme in the pre-training objective, where the coarse-grained experts are responsible for guiding the selection of finer-grained ones based on the input data. We propose variants of teacher-student networks to implement these hierarchical relationships, where teacher experts help student experts narrow down the focus.
CONTROLS: We monitor the expert specialization as a function of depth in the hierarchy and report the performance for both the system as a whole and the experts individually at different layers.
COST: 26920 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The hierarchical structure will effectively compartmentalize the model and avoid the tendency for experts to develop redundant functionalities. Specialization will also be more organized and adapt to different input sub-spaces. Performance will likely improve, but prediction of benefits for more challenging, higher-depth, tasks may be more sensitive to over-specialization.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Regularization-based Orthogonality Promotion
PROPOSAL: To further enhance the expert specialization and structural diversity, we introduce a regularization term to enforce orthogonality of the expert weights, i.e., the coefficients of the expert routing probabilities. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Explicit Objectives for Routing Diversity in Mixture-of-Experts
PROPOSAL: We investigate a combinatorial version of the routing objective, where we add pairwise losses to the original load-balancing loss. Instead of merely promoting uniform expert usage, the new objective encourages diverse combinations of experts across the same token sets, with a target of selecting at least one expert from an optimal partition of tokens given the available experts. We compute the optimal partition via graph clustering.
CONTROLS: We compare to a baseline of standard load-balancing objectives, and ablate our method by considering ablated version of the pairwise losses, all while fine-tuning with the same set of hyperparameters.
COST: 60000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: With this objective, experts are more likely to be trained on non-overlapping data distributions, reducing the incidence of expert homogenization. This in turn should improve language modeling performance and enable more efficient generalization in downstream tasks. I predict a 5% absolute improvement in perplexity on the benchmark evaluation, particularly in tasks with high functional specialization, but also a risky failure mode where the more rigid routing constraints might inadvertently freeze some of the experts and lead to over-specialization for some tasks.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Expert Specialization
PROPOSAL: In addition to the combinatorial routing objective, we introduce a hierarchical structure for the experts. We divide the input space into a hierarchical set of sub-spaces, where each expert in a deeper layer is fine-grained and can specialize in a specific, but smaller subset of the input space. This is defined through a top-down scheme in the pre-training objective, where the coarse-grained experts are responsible for guiding the selection of finer-grained ones based on the input data. We propose variants of teacher-student networks to implement these hierarchical relationships, where teacher experts help student experts narrow down the focus.
CONTROLS: We monitor the expert specialization as a function of depth in the hierarchy and report the performance for both the system as a whole and the experts individually at different layers.
COST: 80000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The hierarchical structure will effectively compartmentalize the model and avoid the tendency for experts to develop redundant functionalities. Specialization will also be more organized and adapt to different input sub-spaces. Performance will likely improve, but prediction of benefits for more challenging, higher-depth, tasks may be more sensitive to over-specialization.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Domain-Agnostic Expert Structure (DAES) Regularization
PROPOSAL: Regularize the experts' weights using a control variate technique that combines soft-k-means clustering and a Lipschitz constant to promote cluster centroids having similar norms, thus encouraging domain-agnostic specialization of experts. This is evaluated during early stages of pre-training and is incorporated into the standard training objective.
CONTROLS: Baseline: standard MoE with load-balancing loss; ablation: different cluster numbers, ratios of cluster centroids to experts.
COST: 1400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: DAES regularization successfully prevents homogenization by promoting diverse, domain-agnostic expert structures, which should translate to reduced interpolation errors in downstream tasks, but may lead to vanishing gradients when the target data distribution shows disparate densities across different domains.

TITLE: Guiding Expert Specialization via Token-Aware Routing
PROPOSAL: We modify the standard MoE routing algorithm to make token-wise routing decisions based on the similarity between input tokens and learned token embeddings. ACTION: ADD 
TITLE:  Explicit Routing Diversity through Total Variation Regularization
PROPOSAL: We explore the idea of incorporating total variation regularization to the routing matrix of the MoE model, which encourages row-wise diversity in the routing patterns, guiding experts to develop distinct specializations and discouraging redundant functionalities. This will be implemented using the Knowledge Distillation framework on Common Crawl, pushing 4 different capacity variations of MoE-LM from 160B to 2400B parameters. The model will be evaluated for diversity metrics, precision-at-k, and correlation analysis with the baselines (Hierarchical routing on monolingual CC + multilingual CC).
CONTROLS: 
1. Baseline: Load-balanced MoE on knowledge distillation, monolingual (CC) and multilingual (CC+40 languages).
2. Ablations: Only monolingual baseline and omitting the TV diversity constraint.
COST: 324000
PREDICTION: It should lead to better divergence and less redundancy among experts but may struggle to maintain the same level of overall performance due to over-specialization, specially noticeable in tasks requiring broader knowledge than possessed by the base models used.

PROPOSAL: We propose a hierarchical routing strategy with domain expertise for large-scale pre-training of MoE models. In this approach, we divide the routing process into two stages: a domain expertise stage, where a low-dimensional representation of the input is used to select a subset of experts with domain-specific knowledge, and a task-specific stage, where a high-dimensional representation of the input is used to select the final expert for each task. ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Modular Multi-Component Trainer (MMCT) for Joint Component Adaptation
PROPOSAL: Implement a modular multi-component trainer (MMCT) that jointly optimizes data augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function over the course of training, adaptively adjusting the configuration in response to the evolving training state. MMCT will use a hierarchical optimization framework, where a high-level controller predicts optimal configuration updates based on the current training state, and a low-level optimizer applies these updates to fine-tune the model. The controller will integrate scripted and learned components to leverage the strengths of both, with a pre-training phase for learning predictive models from past experiments and a meta-learning phase to adapt to new tasks.
CONTROLS: Static configurations using stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with categorical cross-entropy loss, standard robust data augmentation, and a pre-defined learning rate schedule.
COST: 18000
PREDICTION: MMCT will outperform static configurations on real-world multi-label datasets such as CUB-200 and iNaturalist by 2-3% in terms of average precision, and show improved convergence stability and handling of rare labels. However, potential difficulties in scaling up the controller to large models or complex datasets might hinder its effectiveness.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Adaptive Augmentation Search (MAAAS)
PROPOSAL: Introduce Model-Agnostic Adaptive Augmentation Search (MAAAS), an efficient method to adaptively search for effective augmentation strategies during training. MAAAS maintains a separate search space for each model output (feature and score), adaptively searching for augmentation policies that maximize evidence lower bounds (ELBs) on the validation set. The searched augmentation policies will be used to augment both training and validation datasets, effectively adapting to the changing patterns in the input space as the model learns.
CONTROLS: A baseline using static, pre-defined augmentation strategies.
COST: 42000
PREDICTION: MAAAS will show significant performance gains over static augmentation strategies, particularly for models that were previously difficult to optimize, especially on benchmarks like Caltech-101 and Oxford Flowers-102. However, the adaptive nature of MAAAS may make it more prone to overfitting or depend on a specific model architecture.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Loss Weighting (HLW) for Multi-Label Classification
PROPOSAL: Introduce Hierarchical Loss Weighting (HLW), a method for dynamically adapting the loss weights of individual labels in a multi-label classification setting. HLW employs a hierarchical approach, where a selector network predicts the relative importance of each label, and a secondary "weighting" network adjusts the loss weights for each label based on the selector output. This allows for adaptive balancing of the importance of different labels, and enables the model to focus on the most critical labels during training.
CONTROLS: A baseline using fixed label weights and a variant of HLW with only a single fixed weighting network.
COST: 27000
PREDICTION: HLW will improve performance on real-world benchmarks by up to 5% in terms of precision and recall for dense and sparse labels, particularly when dealing with imbalanced label distributions. However, potential challenges in tuning the complexity of the selector and weighting networks may limit the effectiveness of HLW.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Active Learning for Managers of Dynamic Loss Functions (ALDM)
PROPOSAL: Design a new paradigm for handling dynamic loss functions by introducing a meta-learning approach for label acquisition, dubbed Active Learning for Managers of Dynamic Loss Functions (ALDM). ALDM uses a meta-learner to infer the relative importance of each label based on the current model's performance and adapts the loss weights accordingly, while concurrently proposing the most informative labels for human annotation, thereby selectively acquiring new labels to augment the training set. This approach enables dynamic adaptation to evolving loss functions and improves the efficiency of annotation efforts.
CONTROLS: A baseline loss function with static weights, and a variant of ALDM that does not use the meta-learner for label importance inference.
COST: 55800
PREDICTION: ALDM will improve the performance on real-world multi-label datasets by up to 2% in terms of average precision, particularly in scenarios with imbalanced label distributions or decreasing marginal returns. However, the reliance on manual annotation for label acquisition may pose challenges in practice.

TITLE: Navigator-Based MMCT with Predictive Model for Efficient Exploration-Exploitation Trade-off
PROPOSAL: Introduce a Navigator-Based MMCT (NBMMCT) framework that incorporates a predictive model to guide the search process and facilitate an efficient exploration-exploitation trade-off. The predictive model will learn to anticipate the benefits of exploring new configurations based on the model's current performance and will provide adaptive guidance on when to adjust the component configuration. This approach will enable NBMMCT to dynamically balance exploration and exploitation, leading to accelerated convergence and improved performance on multi-label tasks.
CONTROLS: A baseline MMCT and a variant of NBMMCT without the predictive model for adaptive exploration-exploitation.
COST: 102000
PREDICTION: NBMMCT will outperform MMCT and other state-of-the-art multi-label trainers by up to 12% in terms of accuracy, and provide robust performance on complex multi-label tasks with varying degrees of class imbalance. However, potential challenges in tuning the predictive model's hyperparameters and ensuring it remains aligned with the task requirements may limit the effectiveness of NBMMCT.

TITLE: Leaderboard-Based Meta-Learning for MMCT: Adapting Joint Component Optimizers to Novel Tasks
PROPOSAL: Introduce a novel meta-learning approach for MMCT, where a leaderboard-based method is employed to learn optimal component configuration adaptors for joint optimization. By ranking multiple component configurations and their corresponding validation performances, the model will learn to adapt the MMCT framework to different tasks and data distributions. This approach will enable MMCT to exhibit fast and agile adaptation to new, unseen tasks, while maintaining its robustness and accuracy on diverse multi-label datasets.
CONTROLS: A baseline MMCT and a variant of MMCT using a traditional meta-learning framework for optimizer adaptation.
COST: 108000
PREDICTION: Leaderboard-based meta-learning for MMCT will achieve state-of-the-art performance on a range of multi-label datasets, showing consistent improvements over the baseline MMCT by up to 18%. However, careful tuning of the leaderboard weighting method and the MMCT architecture might be necessary to maintain stability and optimality.

TITLE: Provable Safe Adaptation in DJCA
PROPOSAL: Develop a provable safe adaptation strategy for DJCA, leveraging a variant of the non-stationary mirror descent (NSMD) algorithm to ensure the stability and convergence of the adaptive training components. Specifically, design a regularization-term-based NSMD variant to penalize excessive changes in the configuration, and establish a theoretical bound on the progress of the configuration update process.
CONTROLS: (1) The standard NSMD algorithm; (2) A baseline that uses a fixed, predetermined set of configuration updates.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: The provable safe adaptation strategy will improve the stability of DJCA by enforcing a regularized change in the configuration, potentially enhancing convergence rates and reducing the risk of divergence in the adaptive process. However, the delayed adaptation of NSMD may limit its effectiveness in capturing dynamics related to rare labels, potentially leading to suboptimal performance in these areas.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Exploration-Exploitation Trade-offs in DJCA
PROPOSAL: Investigate the exploration-exploitation trade-offs inherent in DJCA's adaptive component updates, by sampling different adaptation frequencies $T_{adapt}$ and leveraging a non-parametric uncertainty estimation (NPE) method to quantify the epistemic uncertainty associated with each adaptive step. Evaluate the impact of these trade-offs on the quality of the discovered configurations, and analyze their effect on the model's performance on rare labels.
CONTROLS: (1) A fixed, predetermined adaptation frequency; (2) A baseline that uses a fixed, uninformed adaptation strategy.
COST: 2520
PREDICTION: Optimizing the exploration-exploitation trade-offs will reveal a sweet spot that balances the exploration of new configurations with the exploitation of high-performing ones, leading to improved performance on rare labels. However, over-exploration can lead to inefficient gains, while under-exploration may cause the model to miss critical configurations, indicating the need for an adaptive strategy to balance these competing pressures.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Transfer Learning and Multi-Component Adaptation
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of transfer learning to adapt multi-label image classifiers from one dataset to another, with a focus on DJCA's multi-component adaptation mechanism. Evaluate the transfer performance of DJCA in different adaptation scenarios, and explore the impact of initial model sizes, adaptation frequencies, and pre-training protocols on the quality of transferred configurations.
CONTROLS: (1) Fine-tuning a single component (e.g., the critics or policy network) of a pre-trained model; (2) Transferring static configuration baselines.
COST: 5400
PREDICTION: By adaptively fine-tuning and coordinating multiple components, DJs with transfer learning can improve the robustness of pre-trained models to new environments and labels, yielding substantial gains over static configuration and fine-tuning baselines. The key may be in adaptively configuring different modules for distinct adaptation scenarios, ensuring effective knowledge transfer from the original to the target environment.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Improved Provable Safe Adaptation in DJCA
PROPOSAL: Refine the existing provable safe adaptation strategy (Proposal 2) by incorporating robust regularizers and incorporating key insights from robust optimization, which can help to quantify and mitigate the impact of uncertain and changing data distributions and labels on the adaptive training process.
CONTROLS: (1) The original NSMD-based adaptation strategy; (2) A baseline that uses a robust loss function to encourage stability.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: By refining the provable safe adaptation strategy to account for the complexities of real-world data, the approach will demonstrate even better stability and robustness across diverse adaptation scenarios, potentially improving overall performance and enabling the adaptation process to converge to better global minima. However, the complexity of the adapted optimization process may introduce additional computational costs, potentially limiting its applicability in very large or high-dimensional problem spaces.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Scalable Hyperparameter Tuning for DJCA
PROPOSAL: Develop an efficient scalable hyperparameter tuning framework for DJCA that leverages Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to guide the search for optimal configurations with reduced computational overhead. The approach integrates existing hyperparameter search techniques with the adaptive component updates, aiming to maximize the efficiency of the overall search process.
CONTROLS: (1) Grid search for hyperparameters; (2) Random search with bandit-based optimization.
COST: 4200
PREDICTION: By combining MCTS with the adaptive training mechanism of DJCA, the framework will find better-valued hyperparameters more efficiently, leading to improved model performance and accelerated adaptation across diverse environments. However, the benefits may be diminished if the computational overhead of MCTS and the existing optimization components is too great, thus requiring additional optimization within the framework itself.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: AutoML for Adaptive Loss Functions in DJCA
PROPOSAL: Design a model-agnostic AutoML framework to automate the search for adaptive loss functions within DJCA, with the goal of maximizing the flexibility and effectiveness of the adaptive training process. This framework integrates existing AutoML techniques with an exploration-exploitation trade-off analysis, allowing it to navigate the challenging search space of adaptive loss functions.
CONTROLS: (1) Standard static loss functions; (2) An ablation study on the role of the AutoML framework in DJCA.
COST: 6600
PREDICTION: By automating the search for adaptive loss functions, the framework will greatly enhance the adaptability of DJCA and potentially unlock its full potential, leading to better convergence rates, higher validation accuracy, and more effective handling of rare labels. However, the complexity of the search space for adaptive loss functions may impose significant computational demands, and the potential for overfitting or underfitting due to the automated selection process must be carefully managed.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Reward Shaping for DJCA with Auxiliary Tasks
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of auxiliary tasks and reward shaping within the reinforcement learning framework of DJCA, with the aim of improving the effectiveness of the adaptive training process and promoting more efficient exploration-exploitation trade-offs. By incorporating valuable information from auxiliary tasks, the framework can learn to balance the exploration-exploitation trade-offs more efficiently.
CONTROLS: (1) Single-criterion reward function; (2) Baseline that uses a static learning rate.
COST: 10200
PREDICTION: By incorporating auxiliary tasks, the modified framework will be able to improve adaptation efficiency, particularly for sparse label distributions, leading to better overall performance and faster convergence. However, the integration of auxiliary tasks may significantly increase the computational complexity of the overall algorithm, imposing strict demands on computational resources and the quality of optimization algorithms used within the reward shaping process.

TITLE: Dynamic Joint Component Adaptation (DJCA) Training
PROPOSAL: Train a multi-label image classifier using DJCA, a novel adaptive technique that integrates and coordinates four core training components: data augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function. DJCA starts with a fixed initial configuration, then uses a reinforcement learning (RL) controller to adjust and synchronize the components every $T_{adapt}$ iterations based on the current performance and learning dynamics.
CONTROLS: (1) Static configuration baseline with DeiT-V3 and Adam optimizer; (2) Adaptive augmentation policy with separate RL control for each component; (3) Ablation study on the hyperparameters of the RL controller.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: DJCA will exhibit faster convergence and higher validation accuracy than the static configuration baseline, particularly on rare labels, and will require fewer iterations to achieve converge, potentially reducing training cost. However, the adaptation frequency $T_{adapt}$ may need to be tuned carefully to balance exploration-exploitation trade-offs and avoid disrupting the learning process.

ACTION: ADD 
TITLE: Adaptive Component Coordination (ACC) via Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
PROPOSAL: Train a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) system where each agent corresponds to a core training component (augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function). Agents interact with each other through information sharing and competitive/ cooperative objectives, learning to adapt their actions in real-time to optimize overall performance. We will train the MARL system on a combination of multi-label image classification tasks across different datasets (CUB-200-2011, NABirds, Stanford Cars).
CONTROLS: Compare ACC to a baseline where components are fixed in advance and a random search for optimal component configurations.
COST: 41.51328
PREDICTION: ACC will show improved handling of rare labels, stable training, and faster convergence than fixed configurations; however, increased computational overhead might hinder its adoption in some scenarios where resources are limited.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Dynamic Configuration Space Exploration via Hierarchical Progressively Bidirectional Neural ODE (HiPinN-ODE)
PROPOSAL: Design a neural ODE model (HiPinN-ODE) that hierarchically explores the configuration space by progressively refining the model's architecture and its component configurations. This is achieved through forward and backward differential equations that act as neural transport processes. The model is trained on a dataset with a large variety of multi-label image classification tasks. 
CONTROLS: Compare HiPinN-ODE to a baseline hierarchical exploration of the configuration space and the existing ACC experiment.
COST: 175 
PREDICTION: The HIpinN-ODE will efficiently explore the highly complex configuration space by exploring competing trajectories and combining real-world constraints allowing for more accurate search for configurations and near optimal convergence rates  but increased training time and interpretability needs might add complexity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ensembling Accelerated Compositional Adaptation (EACA) through Efficient Online Calibration
PROPOSAL: Investigate the ability of ensembling different adaptive components to accelerate compositional adaptation in multi-label image classification. The EACA framework introduces an efficient online calibration step that adjusts the weights of the ensemble members based on their relative performance on a validation set. EACA is expected to outperform static configurations, ACC, and other baselines in terms of accuracy, convergence speed, and robustness to unseen data distributions.
CONTROLS: Compare EACA to ACC, UDKD, HiPinN-ODE, and static configuration baselines on a variety of multi-label image classification benchmarks.
COST: 450 
PREDICTION: EACA has the potential to achieve state-of-the-art performance in multi-label image classification tasks, but its performance may be sensitive to the choice of ensemble members and calibration strategy.

PROPOSAL: Train a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) system where each agent corresponds to a core training component (augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function). ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Automatic Joint Configuration Search and Adaptive Training for Multi-Label Image Classification
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel method called "AutoConfig" that employs a hybrid of Bayesian optimization and multi-objective reinforcement learning (RL) to jointly search for and adapt the core training components of a multi-label image classifier. During training, AutoConfig observes the model's performance metrics and dynamically selects optimization techniques, such as augmentation, optimizer, and learning-rate schedule, in a way that balances exploration-exploitation and maximizes validation performance.
CONTROLS: We compare AutoConfig with static configuration, random search, and state-of-the-art adaptive methods for each individual component, such as Adabelief optimizer or cutmix augmentation.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: AutoConfig is expected to yield significantly better performance and convergence speed than static configuration and other adaptive methods, but may struggle to handle extreme cases where training dynamics are highly nonlinear or unpredictable.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncovering the Interaction Landscape of Multi-Label Image Classification Training Components
PROPOSAL: We design a comprehensive experimentation framework that systematically evaluates the interactions between different training components, including data augmentation, loss functions, learning-rate schedules, and optimizers. Using a set of carefully crafted ablation studies and pairwise comparisons, we aim to uncover the underlying interaction landscapes for various multi-label image classification models and datasets.
CONTROLS: Our baseline configurations will include combinations of popular data augmentations (e.g., RandAugment, CutMix), loss functions (e.g., cross-entropy, focal loss), learning-rate schedules (e.g., step, cosine), and optimizers (e.g., SGD, Adam).
COST: 500
PREDICTION: By shedding light on the complex interplay among training components, our results will help inform the design of AutoConfig and other joint configuration methods, but will also reveal potential pitfalls and challenges that need to be addressed in future work.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing the Generality and Robustness of AutoConfig Across Diverse Multi-Label Image Classification Tasks
PROPOSAL: To gauge the robustness and generality of the AutoConfig approach, we will conduct an extensive set of experiments across diverse multi-label image classification tasks, including those with varying label spaces, image sizes, and class imbalances. We will evaluate AutoConfig on six different benchmarks (e.g., PASCAL VOC, iNaturalist, CIFAR-100) and assess its performance relative to static configuration, random search, and other state-of-the-art methods.
CONTROLS: We will control for the specific hyperparameters used in the AutoConfig approach and compare results with a range of model architectures (e.g., ResNet, DenseNet, U-Net).
COST: 600
PREDICTION: AutoConfig is expected to perform well across different datasets and task domains, but may struggle to adapt to cases with extremely large label spaces or significant class imbalances where specialized meta-learning approaches would be more effective.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Label Complementarity on Joint Configuration Search
PROPOSAL: We will investigate how label complementarity affects the performance of AutoConfig and other joint configuration methods. By using methods such as Cramér's V statistic, we will quantify the label complementarity across datasets and model architectures. We will then use this information to adjust the configuration space explored by AutoConfig and evaluate its impact on final performance.
CONTROLS: We will compare AutoConfig with and without label complementarity-aware configuration search, as well as other methods that explicitly consider label relationships, such as multi-label Structured Prediction.
COST: 533.28
PREDICTION: By accounting for label complementarity, we expect AutoConfig to improve performance and robustness, but the added computational cost may introduce performance degradation on small-scale problems where efficiency is critical.

TITLE: Deriving Sample-Efficient Methods for Joint Configuration Search using Meta-Learning
PROPOSAL: We will propose sample-efficient methods for joint configuration search using meta-learning. By pre-training a meta-model to perform joint configuration search across a variety of tasks and datasets, we can enable efficient adaptation to new tasks and datasets. Using a set of carefully crafted ablation studies and pairwise comparisons, we aim to uncover the underlying interaction landscapes for various multi-label image classification models and datasets.
CONTROLS: Our baseline configurations will include combinations of popular data augmentations (e.g., RandAugment, CutMix), loss functions (e.g., cross-entropy, focal loss), learning-rate schedules (e.g., step, cosine), and optimizers (e.g., SGD, Adam).

PREDICTION: By shedding light on the complex interplay among training components, our results will help inform the design of AutoConfig and other joint configuration methods, but will also reveal potential pitfalls and challenges that need to be addressed in future work.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing the Generality and Robustness of AutoConfig Across Diverse Multi-Label Image Classification Tasks

PREDICTION: By accounting for causal relationships, we expect revised AutoConfig to improve adaptive training and generalizability, but the increased model complexity may introduce challenging optimization and computational bottlenecks if not properly addressed.

We will then use this information to adjust the configuration space explored by AutoConfig and evaluate its impact on final performance.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Adaptive Sampling and Augmentation via Online Learning
PROPOSAL: Implement an online learning framework that trains a classification model to sample and augment data points dynamically, using a probability of selection that's dynamically adjusted based on the performance of the model. Specifically, for a given batch of images sampled from the training set, the model uses a Gaussian process to estimate the probability of a selected image being relevant for the task, based on the model's predictive uncertainty. The model then samples from this distribution to select the next batch of images, applying augmentation techniques tailored to the predicted probability of relevance.
CONTROLS: Compare with static data augmentation using various popular techniques, such as random cropping, color jittering, and flipping.
COST: 2560
PREDICTION: Expected to improve the handling of rare labels by adapting to their varying difficulty, while potentially leading to early stabilization in training. However, it may be challenging to balance exploration-exploitation trade-offs, especially when labels are highly imbalanced, potentially leading to over-fitting to easy labels.

PROPOSAL: Develop a neural architecture that jointly optimizes data augmentation, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, and loss function over the course of training. TITLE: Safety-Critical Hyperparameter Learning via Multi-Source Monitoring
PROPOSAL: Design a monitoring system that utilizes multiple sources of training information (e.g., epoch-wise validation metrics, intermediate feature representations, and attention distributions during training) to monitor and adjust hyperparameters in real-time. This is achieved through a neural network-based learning framework that continually monitors the trade-offs between convergence speed, model quality, and potential overfitting risks. The monitoring system flags potential hyperparameter adjustments to prevent certain adverse effects during early stages of training.
CONTROLS: Compare with a hyperparameter search approach that ignores these factors, as well as an adaptive optimization method with progressively adjusted learning rates.
COST: 4600
PREDICTION: Expected to mitigate overfitting risks and improve convergence rates by acting on early warning signals before they grow into excessive overfitting. However, depends heavily on suitable source selection and utilized metrics, which may require additional engineering for different models and applications.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Training Configuration Evolution via Infrequent Reweighting and Bias-Reduced Weight Initialization
PROPOSAL: Introduce a locally-weighted optimizer that infrequently reweights the importance of instances within the mini-batch based on the evolving model's predictive distributions and input-specific post-hoc analysis. The reweighting schedule is controlled by a bias-reduced weight initialization phase, which calibrates the magnitude of the initial gradients to stabilizes the optimizer and prevent divergence in weight space. A dual-decomposition of the objective function enables updates to the optimizer weights while preventing interference between objective optimization and reweighting criterion adaptation.
CONTROLS: Compare with the baseline using a static optimizer (e.g., Adam, SGD) and investigate the impact of different reweighting schedules and weight initialization strategies on training convergence and model performance.

PREDICTION: Expected to provide better adaptability to evolving data patterns by leveraging their interplay with the model's predictive uncertainty distributions, potentially leading to more stable training and superior generalization performance. However, its performance and robustness might be impacted by an expertise tradeoff between reweighting accuracy and training convergence velocity.

TITLE: Evaluating Post-Training Quantization for Billion-Scale 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: This experiment evaluates the performance of several post-training quantization methods on the 1.2 billion parameter VGGT model, by applying them to its weights and activations, and evaluating the resulting models on a real-world benchmark such as the Formicarium or DTU datasets, specifically the multi-view reconstruction and camera pose estimation tasks. We consider six post-training quantization methods: 8-bit uniform quantization, 8-bit stochastic quantization, and 4-bit low-precision quantization from the PTQ4ViT and PTQ4DiT papers, as well as their histogram-based variants.
CONTROLS: We run baseline experiments with the full-precision VGGT model as well as with a distilled version of it, which we use as a lower-resolution but faster ablation in some conditions. 
COST: 4000
PREDICTION: We expect high-precision quantization methods to outperform their low-precision counterparts in all tasks, and to be on par with the full-precision VGGT model; most post-quantization variants should retain within ±2% of this baseline, save PTQ4DiT's histogram variant which we might see ovelperfRod +-1%

ACTION rationale: The first step is to confirm whether our chosen quantization methods can adapt to the VGGT model's structure and provide performance gains without compromising accuracy. Given the vast scale of the model, it's also essential to assess our baselines against a distilled, lower-resolution VGGT variant to have a smoother progress towards better designs for concurrent resource constraints

TITLE: Lightweight Calibration for Representative Calibration Sampling in Billion-Scale 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: Since calibration sampling is crucial for correctly quantizing data-independent special tokens and avoiding biased quantization ranges, this experiment aims to develop a lightweight calibration method that efficiently samples a diverse and representative set of calibration scenes. Our approach leverages clustering techniques on.V chromosome sample vector spatial statistics that trait each scene's feature set to extract scene embeddings; the most diverse set of scenes are then selected based on their cosine distances within the embedding space and weighted by each view's entropy to ensure a balanced coverage of semantic space.

PREDICTION: We believe our approach will outperform both competitors and yield a good balance between exploration and time efficiency

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Low-Precision Training for Billion-Scale Transformers
PROPOSAL: This experiment investigates an alternative to post-training quantization: adaptive low-precision training, where the model is trained with low-precision weights and activations from the start. We use a dynamic precision scheduling algorithm to adjust the precision of the model's parameters and activations based on the memory available and the computational resources of the target platform. This approach allows us to achieve a good trade-off between accuracy and efficiency, and to adapt to changing hardware and software environments.
CONTROLS: We compare our dynamic precision scheduling approach to fixed-precision training, and to post-training quantization methods such as ILRR and PTQ4ViT.
COST: 26920
PREDICTION: We expect our dynamic precision scheduling approach to provide better accuracy and efficiency than fixed-precision training, and to be more adaptive to changing hardware and software environments than post-training quantization methods, but with some overhead in training time due to the dynamic scheduling algorithms

TITLE: Efficient Distributed Training for Billion-Scale 3D Reconstruction Transformers
PROPOSAL: To scale up our previous approaches to billion-scale 3D reconstruction transformers, this experiment investigates efficient distributed training methods that can utilize multiple GPUs or TPUs. We propose a gradient compression algorithm combined with parallel filter-wise quantization to reduce communication overhead and speed up the training process. Additionally, we apply a federated learning approach to the calibration process to ensure that each worker node contributes to the overall calibration, improving the robustness and efficiency of the calibration process.
CONTROLS: We compare our proposed approach to state-of-the-art distributed training methods, such as Ring-AllReduce and model parallelism, and to calibration methods that rely on a single worker node.
COST: 50000
PREDICTION: We expect our approach to significantly speed up the training process and improve the robustness of the calibration process, while maintaining good accuracy and efficiency

CONTROLS: We compare our proposed approach to state-of-the-art distributed training methods, such as Ring-AllReduce and model parallelism, and to calibration methods that rely on a single worker node. We also compare our approach to the baseline model without any distributed training or calibration methods.
COST: 180000
PREDICTION: We expect our approach to significantly speed up the training process, improve the robustness of the calibration process, and maintain good accuracy while reducing memory usage and energy consumption compared to the baseline model

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploring Uniform Discretization with Selective Calibration
PROPOSAL: To mitigate the effects of heavy-tailed activation distributions resulting from data-independent special tokens, we will explore a uniform discretization approach and propose a selective calibration scheme to identify and preserve critical information carried by large values. We modify the quantization range estimation process to consider not just mean and variance, but also estimates of the top-channel percentage affected by extreme outliers. Specifically, we assign the most extreme values to the highest bit-widths, while uniformly discretizing the rest to apply pressure on standard networks to retain key information in smaller features contributing less to the model performance. This method will be contrasted with standard uniform discretization and PTQ.
CONTROLS: PTQ VGGT as a baseline, comparing model's performance on public 3D benchmarks (e.g., ScanNet, IKEA) including camera pose, point cloud and depth maps.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Outperforms PTQ but may still suffer from degradation in point-wise precision (especially with highly complex scenes) if information compressed too aggressively.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Refining Selective Calibration for Multi-View 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Building on the selective calibration mechanism, we will refine the process to better adapt to the unique properties of 3D data. Specifically, we investigate two adaptations: (1) incorporating a bias term to account for non-uniform spatial distribution of samples across different views, and (2) introducing a diversity-based sampling heuristic to select calibration data that better represents the complexity and diversity of real-world 3D scenes. We expand our validation to a broader set of public 3D benchmarks (e.g., ShapeNet, Matterport3D, SUNCG) to study the effectiveness of these adaptations in various scenarios.
CONTROLS: Same as before, with addition of new 3D tasks involving point map and point cloud similarity metrics, e.g., Chamfer distance.
COST: 7200
PREDICTION: Requires smaller compress levels (hence lower information loss) to achieve same accuracy as baseline PTQ (due to better calibration for heavy tails) but potentially accelerates memory savings. However, might experience listwise fluctuation (order effects) in some cases due to decision-making on standards about which samples count.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mixing Quantization with Knowledge Distillation for Robustness and Efficiency
PROPOSAL: We investigate a hybrid approach combining knowledge distillation (KD) with post-training quantization (PTQ). The idea is to first train a teacher model at full precision and then distill its knowledge into a student model, which is subsequently quantized with PTQ. By leveraging the knowledge distilled from the teacher, we aim to improve the robustness of the quantized student network and its ability to generalize to unseen scenes. We experiment with several variants of KD, such as Hinton's original KD and contrastive KD, to see which one complements PTQ best.
CONTROLS: PTQ VGGT as a baseline, with teacher-student KD architectures (both with and without precise topology tuning) contrasted on a variety of 3D benchmarks (e.g., those mentioned in proposal 1).
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: While this may indeed lead to robust, quantized student networks in general real-world cases, overfitting phenomenon becomes more likely in cases where a few similar real-world scenes encountered much earlier in the training at teacher's step cause malicious influence on the optimum located, in absence of more guidelines or proper accommodation suited for complexities that arise in points equivalents to TXDx TL(in General AU-SET/GAS band AHRzes/class in Dry Cone MAD SA)

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Adaptive Spatial-Aware Selective Calibration for Multi-View 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Building on the selective calibration refinement, we will incorporate an adaptive spatial-aware component to address the unique needs of each 3D task and scene. We design a spatial-aware module to analyze the spatial distribution of 3D data and adjust the selective calibration accordingly. Specifically, we use a saliency map-based method to highlight the spatially critical regions and adapt the calibration process to prioritize those areas. We evaluate this approach on a range of 3D tasks, including camera pose estimation, point map and point cloud reconstruction, and compare its performance against previous refinements.
CONTROLS: Evaluates improvements from proposal 1, with expanded validation set (addition of new benchmarks, e.g., SGT and T-LESS).
COST: 10800
PREDICTION: Develops more reliable quantized models by making spatial pretrained neuron fully compressional towide richer observations compared against baseline and mix-driven entities result time bodΣ-str compensated overcoming head-To par/.
    
ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Enhancing Mixing Quantization with KD through Neural Architecture Search (NAS)
PROPOSAL: We propose to enhance the mixing quantization with KD approach by using NAS to search for optimal architectures that best combine quantization with KD. Specifically, we will use a reinforcement learning-based NAS approach to search for the optimal teacher-student weight ratio, activation quantization bit-width, and other key hyperparameters for efficient knowledge distillation and PTQ. This will allow us to discover novel and highly efficient architectures that outperform prior work.
CONTROLS: Evaluates effectiveness of NAS enhancements in combination with mixing quantization in KD, on 3D benchmarks.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Distillation-Based Approach to Handling Data-Independent Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: We will leverage the knowledge distilled from the teacher model to adapt its architecture and better handle data-independent special tokens. Specifically, we modify the teacher-student KD architecture to learn an additional "token-agnostic" feature extractor, which helps to reduce the impact of extreme outliers caused by these tokens. This approach will be contrasted with standard teacher-student KD on a variety of 3D benchmarks, focusing on improvements in point-wise precision and robustness to outliers.
CONTROLS: PTQ VGGT as a baseline, with and without token-agnostic adaptation on benchmark datasets.
COST: 13200
PREDICTION: Demonstrates improvements in accuracy and robustness due to more robust approach to handling heavy-tail special token activation distribution, demonstrating compelling point-wise generalization.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Augmenting PTQ with Adversarial Training for Increased Robustness
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to enhancing PTQ by incorporating adversarial training. Through adversarial attacks, we aim to more accurately assess the model's robustness to outliers and heavy-tailed distributions, allowing for better quantization range estimation. We will apply adversarial training to the teacher model prior to knowledge distillation, and evaluate its effectiveness on a range of 3D tasks.
CONTROLS: Evaluates benefit of adversarial training on teacher model on various 3D benchmarks, comparing with previous selective calibration and mixed quantization/KD approaches.
COST: 70200

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Spatial-Aware Selective Calibration for Multi-View 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Building on the adaptive spatial-aware selective calibration, we will develop a model-agnostic version that can adapt to various 3D architectures without modifying their internal structure. Specifically, we design a flexible spatial-aware module that can be integrated into different models, allowing us to leverage selective calibration across a wide range of architectures. This will enable a more flexible and scalable solution for 3D reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: Evaluates model-agnostic selective calibration on a diverse set of 3D models (e.g., PointNet, DGCNN, GC-Net) and tasks (e.g., point cloud registration, 3D shape classification).
COST: 15600
PREDICTION: Provides a robust and flexible framework that can be adapted to various 3D architectures, enabling a more efficient trade-off between calibration quality and computational resources.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Early Stopping and Pausing Techniques for Adaptive Quantization during Training
PROPOSAL: We investigate the use of early stopping and pausing techniques to adaptively adjust the quantization process during training. By carefully monitoring the model's performance and adaptively pausing or resuming training, we can more effectively combine PTQ with selective calibration or KD. This will enable us to find an optimal balance between model performance and quantization accuracy, and reduce the risk of over- or under-quantization.
CONTROLS: Evaluates the impact of early stopping and pausing on PTQ with selective calibration and KD on 3D benchmarks.
COST: 78000

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Knowledge Distillation Augmented with Attention Mechanisms for Handling Data-Independent Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: We propose to enhance the distillation-based approach with attention mechanisms to better handle data-independent special tokens. By dynamically weighing the importance of each token, we can reduce the impact of extreme outliers and heavy-tailed distributions. This approach will be contrasted with standard distillation and KD on a variety of 3D benchmarks, focusing on improvements in point-wise precision and robustness to outliers.
CONTROLS: PTQ VGGT as a baseline, with and without attention mechanisms on benchmark datasets.
COST: 16800
PREDICTION: Highlights the benefits of attention mechanisms in improving the robustness and accuracy of the distillation-based approach to handling special tokens, offering an efficient way to reduce the risk of over-quantization.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Efficient Adaptive Quantization through Robust Regularization
PROPOSAL: We propose to use robust regularization techniques to adaptively adjust the quantization process during training. Specifically, we will incorporate L1, L2, and L∞ regularization terms to encourage the model to learn more robust and stable representations that are less sensitive to outliers and heavy-tailed distributions. By jointly optimizing the quantization parameters and the regularization terms, we can develop more efficient adaptive quantization techniques that balance model performance and quantization accuracy.
CONTROLS: Evaluates the impact of robust regularization on PTQ with selective calibration and KD on 3D benchmarks.
COST: 90000

Specifically, we will use a reinforcement learning-based NAS approach to search for the optimal teacher-student weight ratio, activation quantization bit-width, and other key hyperparameters for efficient knowledge distillation and PTQ. This will allow us to discover novel and highly efficient architectures that outperform prior work.
CONTROLS: Evaluates effectiveness of NAS enhancements in combination with mixing quantization in KD, on 3D benchmarks.
COST: 54000

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Distillation-Based Approach to Handling Data-Independent Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: We will leverage the knowledge distilled from the teacher model to adapt its architecture and better handle data-independent special tokens. Specifically, we modify the teacher-student KD architecture to learn an additional "token-agnostic" feature extractor, which helps to reduce the impact of extreme outliers caused by these tokens. This approach will be contrasted with standard teacher-student KD on a variety of 3D benchmarks, focusing on improvements in point-wise precision and robustness to outliers.
CONTROLS: PTQ VGGT as a baseline, with and without token-agnostic adaptation on benchmark datasets.
COST: 39600
PREDICTION: Demonstrates improvements in accuracy and robustness due to more robust approach to handling heavy-tail special token activation distribution, demonstrating compelling point-wise generalization.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Augmenting PTQ with Adversarial Training for Increased Robustness
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel approach to enhancing PTQ by incorporating adversarial training. Through adversarial attacks, we aim to more accurately assess the model's robustness to outliers and heavy-tailed distributions, allowing for better quantization range estimation. We will apply adversarial training to the teacher model prior to knowledge distillation, and evaluate its effectiveness on a range of 3D tasks.
CONTROLS: Evaluates benefit of adversarial training on teacher model on various 3D benchmarks, comparing with previous selective calibration and mixed quantization/KD approaches.
COST: 70200

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Model-Agnostic Spatial-Aware Selective Calibration for Multi-View 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Building on the adaptive spatial-aware selective calibration, we will develop a model-agnostic version that can adapt to various 3D architectures without modifying their internal structure. Specifically, we design a flexible spatial-aware module that can be integrated into different models, allowing us to leverage selective calibration across a wide range of architectures. This will enable a more flexible and scalable solution for 3D reconstruction tasks.
CONTROLS: Evaluates model-agnostic selective calibration on a diverse set of 3D models (e.g., PointNet, DGCNN, GC-Net) and tasks (e.g., point cloud registration, 3D shape classification).
COST: 46800
PREDICTION: Provides a robust and flexible framework that can be adapted to various 3D architectures, enabling a more efficient trade-off between calibration quality and computational resources.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Early Stopping and Pausing Techniques for Adaptive Quantization during Training
PROPOSAL: We investigate the use of early stopping and pausing techniques to adaptively adjust the quantization process during training. By carefully monitoring the model's performance and adaptively pausing or resuming training, we can more effectively combine PTQ with selective calibration or KD. This will enable us to find an optimal balance between model performance and quantization accuracy, and reduce the risk of over- or under-quantization.
CONTROLS: Evaluates the impact of early stopping and pausing on PTQ with selective calibration and KD on 3D benchmarks.
COST: 78000

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Knowledge Distillation Augmented with Attention Mechanisms for Handling Data-Independent Special Tokens
PROPOSAL: We propose to enhance the distillation-based approach with attention mechanisms to better handle data-independent special tokens. By dynamically weighing the importance of each token, we can reduce the impact of extreme outliers and heavy-tailed distributions. This approach will be contrasted with standard distillation and KD on a variety of 3D benchmarks, focusing on improvements in point-wise precision and robustness to outliers.
CONTROLS: PTQ VGGT as a baseline, with and without attention mechanisms on benchmark datasets.
COST: 50400
PREDICTION: Highlights the benefits of attention mechanisms in improving the robustness and accuracy of the distillation-based approach to handling special tokens, offering an efficient way to reduce the risk of over-quantization.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Efficient Adaptive Quantization through Robust Regularization
PROPOSAL: We propose to use robust regularization techniques to adaptively adjust the quantization process during training. Specifically, we will incorporate L1, L2, and L∞ regularization terms to encourage the model to learn more robust and stable representations that are less sensitive to outliers and heavy-tailed distributions. By jointly optimizing the quantization parameters and the regularization terms, we can develop more efficient adaptive quantization techniques that balance model performance and quantization accuracy.
CONTROLS: Evaluates the impact of robust regularization on PTQ with selective calibration and KD on 3D benchmarks.
COST: 90000

TITLE: Asymmetric Distillation and Quantization with Attention for Efficient 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: We will extend the attention-augmented distillation approach to incorporate an asymmetric distillation mechanism. By asymmetrically weighting the importance of teacher and student representations, we can more effectively balance the trade-off between knowledge transmission and quantization accuracy. This approach will be contrasted with standard distillation and KD on a variety of 3D benchmarks, focusing on improvements in point-wise precision and robustness to outliers.
CONTROLS: PTQ VGGT as a baseline, with and without asymmetric distillation and attention mechanisms on benchmark datasets.

PROPOSAL: We propose to develop an efficient and flexible vocabulary learning approach for 3D reconstruction tasks. By learning a vocabulary of atomic features and their spatial relationships, we can improve the robustness and efficiency of 3D reconstruction models. We will develop a novel vocabulary learning method that incorporates quantization and attention mechanisms, allowing for efficient and flexible adaptation to various 3D tasks and datasets.
CONTROLS: Evaluates the impact of vocabulary learning on PTQ with selective calibration and KD on 3D benchmarks.
