PROPOSAL: We propose an experiment comparing RAQ, a simple baseline where each layer's activations are randomly converted to low-bitwidth integers (e.g., 8-bit integer), to the full-precision model on a diverse set of multi-view 3D reconstruction benchmarks (e.g., Matterport3DExt, Sun3D).

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Optimal Token-Specific Quantization for Transformers
PROPOSAL: Inspired by previous research on quantization for transformers, we propose a task-specific token quantization approach, where each token (including the camera and register tokens) in the 3D reconstruction transformer is assigned a customized optimal low-bitwidth precision (e.g., 8-bit), optimized to preserve key 3D reconstruction information. We will investigate whether a mixture of precision levels, specifically 4-bit, 8-bit, and 32-bit, for camera tokens, register tokens and image tokens can balance accuracy and quantization level.
CONTROLS: Compare to uniform quantization of tokens (i.e., either all tokens quantized to the same precision) and determine what percentage of tokens tolerated low precision with minimal impact on accuracy.
COST:   2100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This technique should outperform uniform token quantization and randomly assigned precision, as well as reduce the deep sacrificing of accuracy for the sake of simplicity as seen in RAQ.

TITLE: Investigating Weight-Free Tokens and Auxiliary Multi-Head Attention for 3D Reconstruction Tasks
PROPOSAL: We propose modifying the previous experiment to focus on jointly learning weight-free token representations that capture complex 3D scene structures, using an auxiliary multi-head attention mechanism to aggregate global context and improve camera pose estimation accuracy. CONTROLS: Compare our approach to a standard multi-head attention mechanism without auxiliary weight-free tokens and evaluate its performance on various 3D reconstruction benchmarks.
COST: 7680 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Expect our approach to significantly improve camera pose estimation accuracy and overall 3D reconstruction performance, particularly in scenes with complex structures and occlusions.

TITLE: Investigating Visual Tokenizers and Min-Max Normalization for Efficient 3D Reconstruction Transformers

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Special Token Quantization Strategies
PROPOSAL: We propose and experiment with three special token quantization strategies in PTQ for VGGT - (a) Learning-based dynamic scaling, (b) Channel-wise adaptive quantization, and (c) Ordinary Scale on Special Tokens as the control. Each approach aims to tackle the issue of heavy-tailed distributions associated with special tokens. These approaches will be evaluated on a sub-set of the DTU dataset for dense depth estimation and camera pose estimation tasks.
CONTROLS: The orthogonal controls are the variant with PTQ without special token pre-processing, baseline with no PTQ after inference (float backends).
COST: 2250
PREDICTION: We anticipate that a well-designed dynamic scaling strategy can close or even surpass the gap with the full-precision baseline in-depth accuracy. However, Those results may founder if dynamic scaling doesn't properly set distinct low-bits in +method comparison.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Improving Calibration Using Synthetic Multi-View 3D Data
PROPOSAL: To handle the complexity and variability of real-world images, we create a synthetic multi-view 3D dataset (GeoSpora) using a combination of 3D CAD models and synthetic 2D renderings. We then design a calibration procedure that combines data from GeoSpora with a subset of real-world images to create a robust and representative calibration set. This calibration set is then used to fine-tune the PTQ model, aiming to reduce the gap between the PTQ and full-precision VGGT on real-world benchmarks like DTU and CO3D.
CONTROLS: We include three controls: (a) baseline PTQ with no calibration, (b) PTQ with calibration using only real-world images, and (c) PTQ with calibration using only GeoSpora.
COST: 3600
PREDICTION: We expect that the proposed calibration procedure will significantly improve the performance of PTQ on real-world benchmarks, especially for tasks like 3D reconstruction and camera pose estimation. However, results could fail if the synthetic data and real-world data do not capture the underlying distribution of the real-world samples, leading to biased calibration.

TITLE: Investigating Knowledge Distillation for Weight Pruning and Quantization
PROPOSAL: To further reduce the compute requirements of VGGT, we explore knowledge distillation-based weight pruning and quantization techniques. Specifically, we train a lightweight teacher model on a subset of the CO3D dataset, and then use knowledge distillation to prune and quantize the weights of the VGGT model. We evaluate the effectiveness of this approach on the DTU and CO3D benchmarks, comparing it to traditional weight pruning and quantization methods.
CONTROLS: We include two controls: (a) baseline weight pruning using traditional methods, and (b) baseline quantization using PTQ.
COST: 5280
PREDICTION: We expect that knowledge distillation-based weight pruning and quantization will lead to significant reductions in compute requirements while maintaining a high level of accuracy on 3D reconstruction and camera pose estimation tasks. However, results could fail if the lightweight teacher model does not capture the essential features of the VGGT model, leading to poor transfer of knowledge.

TITLE: Quantization-Aware Regularization for Adversarial Robustness
PROPOSAL: We propose a quantization-aware regularization framework to improve the robustness of the VGGT model against adversarial attacks by inducing robustness through knowledge derived from shared special artifacts. We define a loss function that measures the difference between the activations of the quantized and full-precision models under adversarial inputs. By minimizing this loss function during training, we can learn to learn robust representations of the data that are less susceptible to adversarial attacks. We will test this approach on both white-box and black-box attacks and evaluate its efficacy in defending against these threats using a 3D multi-view reconstruction benchmark under high-computer noise.
CONTROLS: Initial Hypothesis on Quantization-based Compression (1), Signature-based Calibration for Special Tokens (2), Dynamic Sample Inclusion and Split Ratio Strategy (3)
COST: 1512
PREDICTION: By effectively regularizing the model to be robust against adversarial attacks, we expect a 25% improvement in the robust accuracy of the VGGT model.

TITLE: Iterative Scaling for Grouped Quantization
PROPOSAL: We propose an iterative scaling framework for grouped quantization, where we first partition the model weights into groups based on their activation statistics and then scale the quantization step sizes for each group adaptively. The scaling process is repeated iteratively, refining the quantization step sizes until convergence. We will evaluate this approach on the VGGT model and compare its performance against state-of-the-art grouped quantization methods. We will use the 3D mesh reconstruction task from the ScanNet dataset to evaluate the accuracy and memory usage of the quantized model.

PROPOSAL: We propose a novel attention mechanism that is specifically designed to handle the challenges of quantization in 3D reconstruction tasks. This mechanism, called Quantization-Aware Attention (QAA), is a variant of the self-attention mechanism that is commonly used in transformer-based models. QAA is designed to adaptively allocate attention weights based on the quantization noise, ensuring that the model can effectively focus on the most informative features while ignoring the noisy ones. We will evaluate QAA on the VGGT model and compare its performance against state-of-the-art attention mechanisms.

TITLE: In-Context Reinforcement Learning with Continuous Posteriors
PROPOSAL: Develop a DPT-style in-context learning model for continuous control tasks by augmenting the vanilla DPT with a continuous action distribution approximated by a normalizing flow. This will enable the model to capture complex, multi-modal continuous action posteriors.
CONTROLS: Vanilla DPT, Standard Policy Gradient Methods (e.g., REINFORCE)
COST: 400
PREDICTION: This approach will demonstrate strong in-context learning capabilities in various continuous control tasks and will provide a solid foundation for further extensions, potentially outperforming standard policy gradient methods on a range of tasks, but may struggle to generalize to completely novel tasks with vastly different reward structures and action spaces.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Empirical Evaluation of Normalizing Flows in In-Context Learning
PROPOSAL: Examine the effect of different normalizing flow architectures (e.g., Real NVP, NAF, Coupling Layers) on the performance of the in-context reinforcement learner with continuous posteriors. Compare these architectures using a suite of simulation benchmarks (e.g., robotic arm control, cart-pole balancing).
CONTROLS: Vanilla In-Context Learner, Random Search for Hyperparameter Tuning
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Some normalizing flow architectures (e.g., Real NVP) will outperform others (e.g., NAF), and the best approach may interact synergistically with specific simulation tasks or settings (e.g., environment complexity, observation/action space), while others may struggle with high-dimensional action spaces or non-linear reward functions.

ACTION: ADD

PROPOSAL: Investigate the interpretability of the in-context learner with normalizing flows through techniques such as attention visualizations, saliency maps, and model interpretability metrics. CONTROLS: Oracle Policy (known optimal policy), Standard Baseline (e.g., REINFORCE)
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: The in-context learner with normalizing flows will demonstrate intriguing interpretability properties, such as identifiable attention patterns and clear signals of exploration-exploitation trade-offs, yet its interpretation may not fully align with oracle policies, and standard baseline methods may appear less coherent or more naive in comparison, hindering overall understanding.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Continuum DPT with Gaussian Mixture Models
PROPOSAL: We introduce the Continuum DPT, a novel extension of the Decision Pretrained Transformer (DPT) architecture, which leverages a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) to model complex, multi-modal continuous action posteriors. This approach enables native action sampling at inference time while preserving the agent's interpretation as posterior sampling. We explore this model on a synthetic dataset comprising challenging robot manipulation and locomotion tasks with varying MDP structures.
CONTROLS: Vanilla DPT (currently available), random action baseline
COST: 1600
PREDICTION: This extension has a high potential for success, as the GMM can effectively capture multi-modal action distributions. Performance across the synthetic tasks should significantly surpass Vanilla DPT. However, this approach might struggle with very high-dimensional observation spaces, potentially causing the GMM to overfit or become computationally expensive.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model Augmentation for Generalization
PROPOSAL: We investigate a novel combination of Continuum DPT with Gaussian Mixture Models (prop 1) and Model Augmentation (MA) techniques to improve the generalization capabilities of the DPT on unseen tasks and parametric variations of known environments. MA injects task-specific information into the DPT through task-agnostic augmentations of the input embeddings. This is done by introducing a learned projection head, which transforms task-specific parameters into augmentations of the input embeddings. We evaluate this modification on a synthetic dataset of robot manipulation and humanoid control tasks.
CONTROLS: Continuum DPT (prop 1) without MA, Vanilla DPT without augmentation
COST: 4400
PREDICTION: This proposal has a high potential for success, given the ability of MA to adapt to unseen tasks. The augmentation mechanism might struggle to generalize in scenarios with drastically changed observation or action spaces, potentially requiring additional architectural complexity. Performance should significantly surpass Continuum DPT without MA, while maintaining strong performance against Vanilla DPT.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hierarchical Inference with Latent Variables
PROPOSAL: We propose a hierarchical inference mechanism for the Continuum DPT with Gaussian Mixture Models (prop 1) and Model Augmentation (prop 2), introducing latent variables to represent the underlying decision-making process of the pretrained DPT. This hierarchical approach enables the agent to explore more abstract representations of the task space, allowing for better adaptation to both seen and unseen tasks. We integrate this mechanism with the Continuum DPT and Model Augmentation from previous proposals and evaluate its performance on a synthetic dataset of robot manipulation and building energy management tasks.
CONTROLS: Continuum DPT + Model Augmentation (prop 2), Vanilla DPT with hierarchy (synthetic tasks)
COST: 12000
PREDICTION: This hierarchical inference mechanism has the potential to improve upon the existing proposals, especially in tasks with complex decision-making processes. However, the additional complexity may lead to overfitting if not properly regularized, requiring careful tuning of hyperparameters. Strong results are expected in tasks with hierarchical structure, but performance may deteriorate in simplified environments.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluation Protocol for In-Context Learning
PROPOSAL: We develop an evaluation protocol for in-context learning in reinforcement learning, focusing on metrics that capture the agent's ability to generalize to unseen tasks and adapt to new situations. Our protocol includes both task-centric metrics (e.g., success rates) and agent-centric metrics (e.g., exploration-exploitation trade-offs). This evaluation framework is designed to be flexible and can be applied to a wide range of in-context learning architectures, including the Continuum DPT and its variants. We validate our protocol on a synthetic dataset of various robot manipulation and humanoid control tasks.
CONTROLS: Existing evaluation protocols, random baseline
COST: 2400
PREDICTION: This evaluation protocol should provide a comprehensive understanding of in-context learning capabilities and facilitate research progress in the field. The protocol's generality and flexibility make it suitable for a wide range of applications, but it might not capture domain-specific nuances.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Temperature Scheduling for In-Context Training
PROPOSAL: We investigate the impact of adaptive temperature scheduling on in-context training in the context of the Continuum DPT and its variants. By iteratively adjusting the temperature used for in-context training, we can fine-tune the balance between exploration and exploitation, enabling the agent to adapt more effectively to novel situations. We develop a series of temperature scheduling strategies, including temperature annealing and temperature cycling, and evaluate their impact on performance using the customized evaluation protocol from proposal 4.
CONTROLS: Continuum DPT, Model Augmentation, and Hierarchical Inference without temperature scheduling
COST: 4800
PREDICTION: Effective temperature scheduling techniques can significantly improve the performance of in-context training, but may also introduce issues such as increased sensitivity to hyperparameters or decreased stability. Performance gains should be particularly pronounced in tasks that require exploration-exploitation trade-offs.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Agent In-Context Learning
PROPOSAL: We extend the Continuum DPT to enable multi-agent in-context learning, where a group of agents can learn and adapt in a shared environment using in-context training. This setting simulates real-world scenarios where multiple agents interact and influence each other's behavior. We evaluate the multi-agent Continuum DPT on a synthetic dataset of robot coordination tasks, using the customized evaluation protocol from proposal 4 and analyzing the impact of temperature scheduling strategies from proposal 5 on agent coordination.
CONTROLS: Single-agent Continuum DPT (prop 1) and temperature scheduling strategies (prop 5)
COST: 28800
PREDICTION: The multi-agent Continuum DPT should exhibit improved coordination and adaptation capabilities compared to single-agent approaches, but may also encounter challenges such as increased computational complexity, social dilemmas, or information overload. Performance should significantly surpass that of single-agent Continuum DPTs, especially in tasks requiring complex coordination and communication.

textes.jumeau:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Meta-Learning for In-Context Transfer
PROPOSAL: We develop a meta-learning framework for transferring in-context learning capabilities across various tasks, leveraging the Continuum DPT and its variants as task-invariant priors. By learning a meta-policy that adapts the Continuum DPT's parameters to new tasks, we aim to facilitate faster and more efficient in-context learning. We evaluate this meta-learning framework on a synthetic dataset of diverse tasks, using the customized evaluation protocol from proposal 4 and combining it with multi-agent learning from proposal 6.
CONTROLS: Continuum DPT, Continuum DPT with model augmentation, and hierarchical inference without meta-learning
COST: 43200
PREDICTION: The meta-learning framework for in-context transfer should significantly accelerate the adaptation process, enabling the Continuum DPT to generalize more effectively across various tasks. However, meta-learning can be computationally expensive, and overfitting to the meta-training distribution is a significant risk. Performance should surpass that of the Continuum DPT and variants without meta-learning, especially in tasks requiring extensive adaptation.
